Group-level voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain and ROI small-volume-corrected tests) are reported with FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates (e.g., DLPFC correlation p(FWE)=0.031), satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This study reports an fMRI experiment with clear visual cigarette cues and within-participant cue contrasts (meets I3 and I4). However, all reported statistical results appear to be ROI-based (a priori anatomically defined ROIs and beta-parameter comparisons); the paper does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual video cues (explicit sexual, erotic, non-sexual exciting, money, neutral). It includes within-subject contrasts of natural reward-related cues (explicit sexual) versus control (exciting) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations and small-volume-corrected ROI results) with coordinates and p-values. Participant age/sex, cue types, task design, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported in the text; MRI acquisition parameters are referenced. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This full text reports an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol cues (handling, pouring, smelling favorite alcoholic drink) and a task contrast of alcohol cues > neutral/control. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain contrasts, coordinates, cluster sizes, p-values, and supplementary tables/figures). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not a truncated abstract). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This study reports task-evoked BOLD fMRI responses to visually presented cues (backward-masked cocaine, sexual, aversive, and neutral images) in cocaine-dependent participants. It includes within-participant contrasts (cocaine vs neutral; sex vs neutral; aversive vs neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds (voxel p<0.005, cluster-corrected p<0.05), with peak coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, MRI parameters (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and statistical methods are described. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (picture blocks) with a within-participant contrast ('alcohol—neutral') and group-level voxelwise analyses reported with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster-extent FWE correction. Results are presented in tables/figures (including supplementary tables) and demographic/MRI/preprocessing details (3T scanner, SPM5/8, sex distribution, age range) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nor non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies all meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study is an event-related task fMRI investigation of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (heroin-related pictures vs neutral pictures). It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts (heroin > neutral) at the first level and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (within-group activations, between-group two-sample t-tests, and voxel-wise correlations) with cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and cue type (visual pictures); participant inclusion/age range is stated and groups were demographically matched. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, or lacking within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts; however, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward cues > control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images) as required by inclusion criterion I4. The reported contrasts compare different cognitive strategies/mindsets (LATER, DISTRACT, ALLOW) against a NOW control mindset while presenting the same food images; these are strategy-related contrasts rather than stimulus-related (food>control) contrasts. The study therefore fails to meet I4, and per the review rules is excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results available in figures/tables), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) specifically apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food vs object images with within-subject food>object contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and small-volume (ROI) corrected results (cluster-based permutation correction), and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, Freesurfer). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity with visual cues and a within-participant SCs vs NCs contrast, and group-level voxelwise statistical maps reported with peak coordinates. However, all reported voxelwise analyses were conducted within an a priori anatomical mask (WFU PickAtlas) and reported at an uncorrected threshold (P<0.001) without applying small-volume correction (SVC) or reporting whole-brain corrected results. Therefore the study effectively reports ROI/mask-restricted results without a qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result, which meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I6 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported), I7 (participant and methods details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated > abstract control stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM99, voxel-by-voxel GLM, group fixed-effects; thresholding reported) with reported activations in reward and attention networks. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. Although the fMRI pilot sample is small, the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-evoked group-level voxelwise results with visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (International Smoking Image Series). It includes within-participant contrasts (smoking > neutral) at the first level and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses with voxelwise threshold p<0.005 and cluster extent correction, reported clusters/tables). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM12), satisfying reporting preferences. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study using visual cannabis cues in adolescent cannabis users with a within-participant cannabis > non-cannabis contrast. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected results (z thresholds and corrected p-values reported) and presents activation clusters (tables/figures/supplementary figures). Participant demographics, cue type (active/passive), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT, FLAME) are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in cannabis-dependent humans using visual stimuli (33-ms images) including drug (cannabis) and natural reward (sexual) cues presented via a backward-masking paradigm. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis>neutral; sexual>neutral; aversive>neutral) at the group level. Voxelwise results are reported within an a priori ROI mask with small-volume (ROI) correction and cluster-level correction; peak coordinates and T-values are provided (Table 2) and figures display activation maps, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), cue types, and participant sex; core manuscript sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using a multimodal taste paradigm that includes explicit visual labels (‘‘Alcohol Taste’’ vs ‘‘Control Taste’’), satisfying the requirement for visual cue content. It reports a within-participant Alcohol versus Water contrast (Alcohol>Water) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain, cluster-corrected results (tables, figures, MNI coordinates). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/SPM procedures) are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain analyses are present; not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of natural-reward (high-calorie food) cue-reactivity using exclusively visual stimuli, reports within-subject contrasts (high-calorie > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie), and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (Z>2.3, p<0.05 corrected). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), imaging parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, SPSS) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a visual alcohol cue-reactivity task (alcohol images vs soft-drink images) with a within-subject contrast (alcohol>soft drink). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (exploratory whole-brain SPM8 results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected findings), and anatomically defined ROI analyses (amygdala/ventral striatum) are reported. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 software, participant characteristics (male subjects, matched groups), and cue type. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject cue (smoking) > neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (familywise error and cluster-corrected results) identifying cue-reactive clusters, with results described in the main text and supplementary materials. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and statistical software (FSL, FILM) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes the required within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). The abstract confirms this is a functional MRI study using virtual-environment smoking cues, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity with a visual component) appears satisfied. However I cannot confirm key required criteria from the available text: I4 (presence of at least one within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast) is not reported in the abstract; I5 (at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result) is not clearly reported—the abstract only mentions detected regions without specifying voxelwise/group-level/statistical reporting); I6 (reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement) cannot be confirmed from the abstract; I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) is partially met (age described as "late-adolescent") but key MRI/method details are missing. Because full text is incomplete and essential inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be verified, I exclude the study pending access to the full article. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I4, I5, I6, I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual beverage cues (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) presented in a block-design visual task, meeting the review objective. The study reports within-participant contrasts of each stimulus versus a mosaic baseline (i.e., cue>control contrasts). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (second-level full-factorial ANOVA) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates reported. Voxelwise results are available in the main text/figures (regions, coordinates, F-values). Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing with SPM12/MATLAB). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text reports an fMRI study using visual alcohol-related pictures and neutral control images (visual cue component). The primary analyses include within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral stimuli and anticipation of monetary gain/loss > no outcome. Group-level voxelwise results are reported, including small-volume-corrected (S.V.C.) analyses in the ventral striatum (p < 0.05 FWE for VOI) with stereotactic coordinates. Results and methods (subjects, MRI field strength 1.5T, preprocessing, SPM2) are fully described. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (participant and acquisition details reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study assesses fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-participant contrasts (food > nature), and reports participant demographics and MRI methods. However, the full text does not present or reference any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (e.g., tables of coordinates or whole-brain group t-maps). Analyses rely on ROI extractions and participant-level contrast maps used for pattern expression; no qualifying group-level voxelwise results are reported. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI/participant-level pattern analyses without a qualifying voxelwise group-level result). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (group-level voxelwise result). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes visual stimuli (pictures) and olfactory cues. It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., HFHS>NF, HFHS>LFLS) and group-level voxelwise pre- to post-surgery T-tests using a whole-brain approach (p=.001 uncorrected, cluster threshold), with reported significant clusters and extracted beta values. MRI field strength (3T), participant demographics, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL) are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual monetary cues (images of coins) and within-subjects contrasts comparing high-value vs low-value cues (Euro > Cent). Group-level voxelwise analyses were reported with whole-brain cluster-level inference (FWE-corrected) and results are presented in figures/tables. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues with a within-subject ALC>BEV contrast, but all imaging analyses are ROI-based: a priori 6-mm spherical ROIs were reverse-registered, average ROI timecourses extracted, and hierarchical linear models run on ROI averages (Bonferroni correction across five ROIs). The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (neither whole-brain nor small-volume-corrected voxelwise maps or cluster coordinates) that would qualify under I5. Therefore it fails the requirement for voxelwise evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual heroin-related cues with a within-participant heroin-related > neutral contrast, whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM8) with multiple-comparison cluster correction, and full reporting of methods, participants, MRI field strength, preprocessing and software. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (colored circles paired with monetary images) in an appetitive conditioning paradigm. It includes within-participant contrasts of CS+ versus CS− (natural reward-related cues vs control) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (PLS voxel saliences, bootstrap ratios, tables of coordinates and figures). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99, MELODIC, AFNI, Amos), and participant demographics. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (palatable food pictures vs. scrambled controls). It includes a within-participant contrast of food>control and reports group-level voxelwise GLM results with small-volume FWE-corrected ROI analyses (right amygdala effect reported, p_FWE=.006). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), stimuli, preprocessing, and SPM5 analysis are described. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrast, and qualifying voxelwise (small-volume-corrected) results. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual cocaine cue videotapes (meets I3). The analyses include within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine cue viewing to a neutral baseline (first 30 s and full 3 min), satisfying I4. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: whole-brain voxelwise correlation analyses and between-group voxelwise contrasts with clusters and Talairach coordinates displayed in tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results (I5, I6). Participant demographics (age/sex distribution), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical methods are reported, meeting I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), and include within-participant cue>control contrasts (E5 not met). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis.

Full text is not accessible (page unavailable); only title/metadata are available. Unable to verify whether the study is a functional MRI task with visual cues, whether it includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, or whether it reports qualifying voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) group-level results. Therefore I cannot apply required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, or I6. No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available information. Because the core article content (methods/results) is missing, fulltext_incomplete is set to true and the study must be excluded from the review at this screening stage pending retrieval of the full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and reports within-subject contrasts of drug cue > neutral. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (voxelwise threshold z>=2.3, cluster-corrected at P<0.05) with reported peak coordinates and cluster assignments; percent BOLD signal change and predictive-value calculations are presented. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing software (FSL), and relevant subject demographics are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (visual cue component, within-participant drug>control contrast, qualifying group-level voxelwise results, coordinate reporting, and methodological details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI pharmaco-study in alcohol-dependent patients using visual alcohol cues. It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral cues (task-evoked GLM contrasts at t1 and t2) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume corrected (SVC, FWE) coordinates (e.g., VS, OFC, Amygdala, VTA). Coordinates and statistical thresholds are provided; MRI field strength (3T), participant demographics, cue type, and software (SPM12) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is a task-evoked human fMRI study of tobacco (drug) cue-reactivity using visual videotaped cues. The study reports within-subject contrasts of cigarette cues > neutral cues (e.g., cigarette cue crave minus neutral; cigarette cue resist minus neutral) at the group level using voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) with voxelwise thresholds (Z>2.3, cluster p=0.01), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Core article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present and participant/sample details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in heavy-drinking participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > rest/control, reports group-level voxelwise results (one-sample and ANOVA) with whole-brain FWE-corrected findings (right inferior frontal gyrus) and a small-volume (ROI) FWE-corrected result in the ventral striatum; peak coordinates and cluster sizes are provided. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics. Therefore all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity voxelwise task-evoked results are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (favorite-food) cue-reactivity but uses individually tailored auditory guided-imagery scripts (audiotaped personalized scripts) rather than visual cues; no visual stimulus component or multimodal design including visual cues is reported. Thus inclusion criterion I3 (clear visual cue component) is NOT met. The study does meet I4 (within-participant contrast: favorite-food vs neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses with FWE correction), I6 (results presented in tables/figures), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I3.

This fMRI study used visual drug cues (opioid words) in an opioid-word Stroop task (I3). A within-participant OW>NW contrast (opioid words vs neutral words) was computed at first level and entered into group-level SPM voxelwise analyses (I4). The paper reports voxelwise second-level task-evoked statistical results (one-sample and two-sample SPM analyses) with cluster-level FWE-corrected findings for the between-group contrast (thus satisfying group-level voxelwise reporting; I5). Results and contrasts are reported in the main text and figures/tables (I6). Participant/sample, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, AFNI) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task-evoked voxelwise results, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using explicit visual smoking and neutral cue pictures and a within-participant smoking>neutral cue contrast. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported: small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (SCC/PCC; SPM small-volume FWE-P values reported) and exploratory whole-brain cluster-level FWE results for cue-induced activations. The paper provides participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CONN), and includes sufficient methods, results, and discussion. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies with qualifying group-level voxelwise results.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in smokers using visual smoking-related and matched neutral images (meets I3). The authors modeled within-subject event types (smoking vs non-smoking/neutral) and generated t-contrast images and random-effects (group-level) voxelwise analyses comparing cue conditions (meets I4). Results are reported as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistics (SPM2 second-level random effects, uncorrected p<0.0001, cluster threshold, with reported activation clusters and a table; meets I5 and I6). Key methodological details are provided (participant sex, cue type, MRI field strength 1.5T, preprocessing and SPM2 software), satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The full text reports an fMRI task using visual smoking and matched neutral images (I3). Analyses include within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral (I4). A group-level voxelwise analysis restricted to the PCC was performed with cluster-level correction using nonparametric permutation testing (z=3.1, p<0.05), which satisfies the requirement for a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result (I5). Relevant voxelwise results are presented in figures/supplementary materials (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported in Methods (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only (it includes voxelwise PCC analysis), not limited to connectivity or resting-state analyses, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual smoking-related images and a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast, with group-level voxelwise results (cluster-corrected Z=2.3, p<0.05) presented in tables and figures. Participant demographics, MRI acquisition parameters, preprocessing, and statistical methods are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity that includes clear visual cues (pictures) within a multimodal paradigm and reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., cannabis picture > baseline; cannabis picture > flower picture). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected; z≥2.3, p<.05) are reported, and a-priori small-volume (ROI) analyses (VTA, nucleus accumbens, pallidum) are also presented. Results are reported in the main text, figures, and tables; participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/AFNI/ANTS) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related pictorial cues in a within-subject design (non-abstinent vs. abstinent), with explicit smoking>neutral contrasts. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain mixed-effects results are reported (significant occipital–temporal clusters with corrected p<0.05; Table 1), and region-specific results within a ventral striatum/nucleus accumbens anatomical mask are reported (bilateral NAc activation reported at p<0.05). Coordinate tables and figures are provided. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and statistical software (FSL, FEAT/FLAME) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smokers viewing visual pleasant, unpleasant, neutral, and cigarette-related pictures (visual cue component). The analysis includes within-subject contrasts (cigarette-related, pleasant, unpleasant > neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level GLM results with FDR correction and cluster thresholds; results are presented in tables and figures with coordinates for significant clusters. Preprocessing details and statistical software (BrainVoyager) and many MRI acquisition parameters are reported; MRI field strength (e.g., 3T) is not explicitly stated in the provided text (I7 is preferred, not mandatory). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smokers using visual smoking videos as cues, with a within-subject contrast of smoking>neutral videos. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain corrected p<0.05 and T-maps/coordinates), and provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and analysis software (fmristat). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol vs control images presented during a combined stop-signal task. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol and control picture trials (e.g., CRAlcohol - CRControl and GOAlcohol - GOControl) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected, tables of MNI coordinates are reported). Participants’ age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related images (visual cue component) and includes within-participant contrasts of smoking-related > neutral images. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction (cluster-corrected p ≤ .005) and details preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager) and MRI field strength (3T). Behavioral Stroop and ICA connectivity analyses are also present but do not replace the task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant sex (women-only) is reported; other descriptive details (age) are not emphasized in the provided excerpt but I7 is preferred not required. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related vs neutral images) with within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral) reported. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected, tables/figures with coordinates) analyzed at the group level using Brain Voyager QX on a 3T scanner. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue reactivity using visual cigarette-related images. It reports within-subject contrasts comparing smoking (craving) versus neutral pictures (craving>neutral) and other task contrasts. Results are presented as voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim/FWE-equivalent) and reported peak coordinates and tables. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and SPM8 statistical software. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and supplementary details). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual smoking video cues and reports task-evoked voxelwise results for the smoking > neutral contrast. It includes a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral), whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with reported peak coordinates/z-statistics) and ROI follow-up, and reports key methodological details (participant ages, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software: FSL). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual picture cues (cocaine and food) with within-participant contrasts (cocaine>neutral; food>neutral). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction and small-volume correction for the hypothalamus; coordinates and cluster statistics are described in the text/figures. Participant demographics and analysis software (SPM) are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for visual cue reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and voxelwise whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual picture stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > beverage control cues (AUD group alcohol–beverage comparison) and group-level voxelwise results analyzed with SPM99, with cluster-level corrected P < 0.05 and Talairach coordinates reported (Table 3 and figures). MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99), participant descriptors (right-handed male and female college students, AUD vs controls), and cue types (alcoholic, non-alcoholic, control pictures) are reported. Full article text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study limitations). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues vs neutral/control images with a within-participant contrast (alcohol > control). Group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain task effect with FWE correction) and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the ventral striatum are reported; results are presented as maps/tables and described in the text. Key participant details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (factorial 2×2 medication × time, with cluster-level inference and tables/figures of results and supplementary tables), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/SPM12), participant demographics (male, age range), and cue type, meeting reporting preferences. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. It includes a within-participant contrast of food images > blurred visual baseline, reports voxelwise group maps and coordinate tables for within-group and between-group contrasts, and states that a whole-brain FDR-corrected analysis was performed. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue component (I3), within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), group-level voxelwise results/whole-brain analysis (I5), reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures (I6), and provides participant and MRI details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (drug images, drug-use tools, drug-use actions) with matched neutral images. It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Action vs. C_Action, Drug vs. C_Drug) and a group-level random-effects 2×2×3 ANOVA with whole-brain voxelwise results, using cluster-level FWE correction (p<0.001) and reporting peak coordinates. Preprocessing and statistical software (SPM12, CAT12), MRI field strength (3T), and participant demographics are described. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-evoked voxelwise visual cue-reactivity results.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation of smoking using visual stimuli and a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast, and reports participant demographics and scanning details. However, group-level results are presented as ROI-based averaged parameter estimates from 5-mm spheres and subsequent ANOVAs rather than as voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates. No qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results are reported in the main text or tables, so the study reports only ROI analyses and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual smoking cues), I4 (within-participant smoking>neutral contrast), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, and software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study is excluded from the voxelwise meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to natural reward-related cues (palatable food) and includes a visual cue paradigm (food pictures) and visual cue shapes signaling milkshake delivery, meeting the review’s focus on visual cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts (appetizing food > unappetizing food; appetizing food > water; milkshake cue > tasteless cue; milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt). Group-level voxelwise results were analyzed with small-volume correction (SVC) and peak coordinates are reported; statistical methods (SPM5) and MRI field strength (3T) and participant demographics are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study using visual cannabis-related, neutral, and positive images (visual cue component). It includes within-participant contrasts (cannabis vs neutral; cannabis vs baseline) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE-corrected coordinates (e.g., right amygdala x=36,4,-30 pFWE=0.006; thalamus/insula results). Core methodological details are provided (male participants age 18–30, 3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI with qualifying voxelwise SVC results. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is a PET (H2[15]O) neuroimaging study, not an fMRI study. The meta-analysis objective explicitly targets fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). Therefore the primary inclusion criterion requiring use of functional MRI is not met. Study strengths relevant to the review: it used within-participant contrasts of drug video > neutral video (I4), reported group-level voxelwise task-evoked SPM results with whole-brain and corrected findings (I5,I6), and provided participant demographics, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software details (I7). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete. Final decision: EXCLUDED due to modality mismatch (PET vs required fMRI).

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli (videos in Study 1 and still images in Study 2). Both studies use within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking control stimuli. Study 1 reports voxelwise group-level GLM results within an a priori ROI mask with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-size correction (i.e., small-volume/ROI-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results) and provides MNI coordinates; Study 2 provides ROI beta extractions and group comparisons and correlations. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM/FSL) are reported. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

This study meets the review objectives and inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI task study of natural (monetary) reward-related cue-reactivity using explicit visual cues (shapes on the MID and visual faces in the probabilistic reward task). It reports within-subject contrasts of reward-cue>neutral (Reward Cue–Neutral Cue) and loss-cue>neutral (Loss Cue–Neutral Cue). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction are reported, and small-volume/ROI analyses were also performed; results are presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistics are described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an fMRI task-based study using visual backward-masked cues (cocaine and sexual images) in human participants. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine vs. neutral; sex vs. neutral) and group-level voxelwise SPM results with cluster- and peak-level statistics and MNI coordinates. Visual stimuli are the primary cue modality. Methods report participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM2 analysis parameters. Voxelwise task-evoked results are presented in text/figures and described with thresholds and corrected p-values, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected evidence. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural rewards (food) using visual food images and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images). The main within-subject contrasts compare food images with vs. without calorie information (two types of food cues) rather than food cue > control stimuli; therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. The study does satisfy I3, I5, I6, and I7, and it is a complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply to this manuscript.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) comparing heavy and light drinkers. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol versus neutral pictures (and other categories) and planned comparisons showing alcohol>neutral effects in heavy drinkers. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects ANOVAs with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction; Talairach coordinates and cluster sizes are reported (Table 2, figures). MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics software (BrainVoyager QX) are described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The study is an fMRI investigation of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual cues and reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps for task contrasts (Attend vs Regulate). However, the paper does not present a qualifying within-participant voxelwise contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., CS+ > CS−) at the group level. The primary reported imaging contrast is Attend CS+ vs Regulate CS+ (instruction effect), and ROI/extraction analyses are reported for dACC. Because the meta-analysis requires at least one within-subject drug-cue>control voxelwise result, this study does not meet inclusion criterion I4 even though it meets other requirements (visual cues, group voxelwise maps, figures/ROI reporting, and participant details). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: E4 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported). This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cues with a clear visual component (I3 satisfied) and includes within-participant contrasts of high-ED > low-ED food cues (I4 satisfied). The paper reports group-level seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity maps (voxelwise connectivity results), but does not present a qualifying task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected activation contrast (high>control) in this manuscript; the authors state main BOLD activation results are reported elsewhere. Participant/sample and acquisition/preprocessing details are reported (I7 satisfied). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4, and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual picture cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, and IAPS emotional pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (e.g., alcohol>neutral, polydrug>neutral, marijuana>neutral). Analyses were performed as group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistics using FSL/FEAT (mixed-effects OLS) with results presented in tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (food images) in adolescents. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of appetizing food images > unappetizing foods and > glasses of water, and describes group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (task-evoked contrasts) for these image-based contrasts (null results reported). The methods specify visual cue paradigms, preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, AFNI), and participant demographics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Thus the study meets criteria for (I3) visual natural reward cue, (I4) within-participant cue>control contrasts, (I5) group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported, and (I6) acceptable reporting of results. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria. It uses visual smoking cues (control vs smoking images) in a cue-reactivity fMRI task (I3). First-level within-participant contrasts of smoking cue > neutral blocks were computed and used in group analyses (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (group × time interactions in rACC and ventral striatum) with cluster-level correction procedures described, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (I5). The manuscript also reports cue type, MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, conn14), meeting preferred reporting elements (I7). Although the sample is small and nonrandomized (limitations noted), none of the exclusion criteria (ROI-only results, connectivity-only without task results, only between-group contrasts without within-subject cue>control contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study investigates appetitive (natural reward: liquid food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures) and reports within-subject CS+ > CS− contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed in SPM12 with small-volume correction (amygdala, NAcc, vmPFC) and reported peak coordinates and corrected p-values, satisfying voxelwise result reporting. Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective (natural reward visual cue reactivity) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues (cue-reactivity task with smoking-related pictures vs neutral) and reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts. The paper provides whole-brain, cluster-wise corrected voxelwise results (cluster-wise thresholding using Monte Carlo simulation/3dClustSim) and shows brain maps/contrast results and coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only (it includes task-evoked whole-brain results), and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-evoked, within-subject BOLD fMRI study in smokers using visual cues (cigarette, pleasant, unpleasant, neutral pictures). It reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrast (cigarette > neutral) with tabulated cluster coordinates and figures (Table 2, figures), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain reporting. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager), and participant demographics (age/sex), and clearly include within-participant cue>control contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues and reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral. Methods describe group-level voxelwise (random-effects second-level) analyses with whole-brain thresholding (p<0.001, cluster ≥10) and report regional activations in tables and figures (coordinates provided). MRI field strength (1.5 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Participant characteristics (age eligibility, smoking history, n=20) and cue type (ISIS smoking vs neutral images) are provided. Although sex breakdown is not explicitly stated in the provided text, omission of a single demographic detail does not preclude inclusion per I7. All primary inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical human fMRI study (pCASL on a 3T scanner) that used audiovisual smoking cues (multimodal design including a clear visual component) and a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > nonsmoking cues. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported, with small-volume correction (SVC) applied to a priori ROIs; peak coordinates and cluster statistics are provided in tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, ASL toolbox) are reported. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food and scenery images). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie and food > scenery) and group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (TFCE, p<0.05 FWER after SVC) including MNI coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength, preprocessing and software. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol images and a within-subject alcohol>pleasant contrast. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (left caudate cluster with MNI coordinates, Z-value, and cluster extent) and whole-brain analyses, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant age/sex and cue type are provided; MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are indicated as available in supplemental materials. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

Although this fMRI study uses visual alcohol cues (alcohol and food images) and reports task-evoked voxelwise results (e.g., regulation contrasts and parametric covariation of brain activity with craving, with small-volume correction for VS/vmPFC), the paper does not report a within-participant voxelwise contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol > neutral/food) at the group level. Inclusion criterion I4 (explicit within-participant drug-cue > control contrast) is not met based on the full text provided. Therefore the study cannot be included for a meta-analysis specifically targeting cue-reactivity contrasts, despite meeting other criteria (I3, I5, I6, I7).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cigarettes, money, neutral) in daily smokers. It includes within-participant contrasts (tobacco>neutral and money>neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (voxelwise one-sample t-tests for disjunction mask with AlphaSim cluster correction, and a priori small spherical ROIs), with results described in the main text and supplementary materials. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), stimulus details, and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) with a within-participant contrast of ‘favourite drinks > neutral’ reported. The paper reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain: P<0.001 uncorrected) and small-volume-corrected ROI results (P<0.05 SVC/FDR) with coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of opioid-use disorder that used visual drug-related cues (drug, sexual, aversive, neutral) and reports within-subject contrasts (drug vs neutral) across sessions. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (whole-brain ANOVA with corrected cluster reported), and ROI small-volume analyses were also presented. The paper reports participant demographics, cue types, 3T MRI acquisition and SPM8 preprocessing/statistics. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary appendices are referenced but core content is present.

This study is excluded because it does not include a visual cue component required by I3. It used olfactory (ethanol odor) stimulation rather than visual cues. The full text is complete and the study does meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast: ethanol odor > neutral air), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain fMRI results reported), I6 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (visual cue component). Exclusion IDs met: none.

This is a human fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast of food>scenery. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (thresholded t-maps, cluster correction, peak coordinates), and interaction analyses were performed; results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps and peak coordinates (qualifying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results). Participant demographics (age, male-only), MRI field strength (1.5T), imaging parameters, preprocessing, and analysis software (fmristat) are reported. The paradigm uses visual-only stimuli (food pictures) and includes the required task-evoked contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material presence is noted but not required. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7.

The fMRI component used visual drug-word cues and included within-subject contrasts (drug>fixation and drug>neutral), satisfying I3 and I4. However, fMRI results are presented as ROI extractions and group-level ANOVAs rather than as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results; no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise coordinates/clusters are reported in the text. Although whole-brain interaction testing is mentioned in methods, no qualifying voxelwise results are provided. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result) and fails to meet I5. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual alcohol cues (with a sip prime) and includes within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol vs beverage and alcohol vs control. Whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected) with tables/figures of activated regions (e.g., nucleus accumbens, insula, cingulate). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM96, MEDx3.3) are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related pictorial cues and neutral control images, with within-participant contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) reported. The paper provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-corrected statistics (Z>2.3, cluster p<.05) for SR vs N contrasts in smokers, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. ROI analyses of the ventral striatum are also reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is an original human fMRI study). Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The full text reports an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli and within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), but imaging analyses are reported as ROI-based percent signal change from anatomically defined ventral striatum spheres rather than as group-level voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) results or coordinate tables. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of anticipation to visual natural-reward stimuli (erotica/romance) versus neutral (everyday) and aversive (violence) scenes. Colored visual cues signaled upcoming picture content, and the authors report voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ANOVA and pairwise contrasts) with cluster results and coordinates indicating increased BOLD for anticipating romance > everyday. Imaging parameters (3T scanner), preprocessing (AFNI), and participant demographics are reported. Thus the study meets the review’s requirements for (I3) visual natural reward cue-reactivity, (I4) within-participant natural reward>control contrast, (I5) group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain), (I6) voxelwise results reported, and (I7) basic methodological details reported. Full text is complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol vs non-alcohol photographs as distractors. It reports within-participant AD> (vs) NAD contrasts (AD-NAD) and voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (rmANOVA) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE) as well as voxelwise correlational analyses; an a priori amygdala ROI analysis is also reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SPM5) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (craving and aversive smoking-related images) in smokers and non-smokers. It includes within-participant contrasts of craving>control and aversion>control (Cr vs mosaic, Av vs mosaic). Group-level voxelwise random-effects GLM results are reported (FDR-corrected maps and region coordinates/BA descriptions), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Methods report participant sex/age group (male), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (Brain Voyager, GLM/RFX), meeting reporting preferences. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of natural reward cues (food) that includes a clear visual cue component (appetizing vs unappetizing food images). The study reports within-participant contrasts of appetizing>unappetizing food images and milkshake cue contrasts, and conducts group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinates and FWE-corrected thresholds. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue>control contrast, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study is an fMRI investigation of smoking cue-reactivity using visual photographic cues, reporting within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > control cues) and group-level voxelwise results. Methods report whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with explicit thresholding (p≤0.001 uncorrected, cluster extent ≥20 voxels) and tables/figures of activations; scanner field strength (4.0 T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM5) and participant demographics are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets the review objective and required analysis/reporting criteria.

Study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI investigation of drug (cigarette) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (participants held and viewed a cigarette via a live video feed) and uses within-participant contrasts (cigarette cue > control cue). Analyses were conducted at the group level using voxel-wise, two-level random-effects GLM and whole-brain inference with cluster-wise correction (AFNI AlphaSim), and results (cue effects and ambivalence-related voxelwise correlations) are reported in the main text/tables, satisfying requirements for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using visual presentation (participants held and viewed cigarettes vs neutral objects). The analysis includes within-subject contrasts of cigarette vs neutral cues (cue main effect and instruction×cue interaction) reported as voxelwise group-level results with tables/figures (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; coordinates in Tables 2–3). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (NIS, AFNI). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine-related pictures and a blocked cue task, with within-subject contrasts computed (Cocaine > Neutral) for each session. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM8 with ROI small-volume FWE-corrected results reported (e.g., VTA/SN FWE-corrected), and coordinates/t-values are presented in the text. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant details are reported. Thus the study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for visual cue-based fMRI cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity that used visual cue exposure (participants held and viewed a cigarette via live video) and a control cue (roll of tape). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts (cigarette vs. control) entered into group-level voxelwise GLMs and a 2×2 ANOVA, with Monte Carlo cluster correction; results are reported as whole-brain coordinates in tables and figures. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (AFNI, FSL, etc.), participant age/sex, and cue type are provided. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images (meets I3) and includes within-participant food>control contrasts entered into second-level analyses (meets I4). Participant/sample and MRI details are reported (female dieters, 3T scanner, preprocessing with SPM8), satisfying I7. However, the manuscript reports results primarily as ROI- and system-averaged ROI analyses (VS, OFC, and aggregated network ROIs) and ANOVAs on extracted beta values. I find no reported group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical voxelwise results (no cluster coordinates or SVC results presented for task-evoked contrasts). Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and fails the required I5 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E3; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7; unmet: I5.

This is a resting-state fMRI study that used an event-related visual cue exposure paradigm only to measure subjective craving (pre/post), but it does not report any task-evoked voxelwise fMRI contrasts of drug cues > control stimuli. Therefore it does not provide the required within-participant cue>control task activation results or group-level task-evoked voxelwise statistics needed for inclusion. The paper reports demographics and methodological details (age/sex, MRI strength, preprocessing), but the imaging results are resting-state connectivity comparisons across groups rather than task-evoked cue-reactivity. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only resting-state analyses reported without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (reports group comparisons without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant and methods reporting). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI cue-reactivity analysis to visual drug cues), I4 (no within-participant drug cue > control contrast), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result). Full text appears complete.

This study used a gustatory (taste) cue-exposure paradigm (alcohol taste vs. litchi juice control) rather than visual cues. Although it includes a within-participant alcohol>control contrast (I4) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I5) with results available in text/tables/figures (I6) and provides participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details (I7), it fails inclusion criterion I3 (clear visual cue component). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual word cues (alcohol-related words vs neutral words). The study reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses (independent-samples t test and single-sample t tests) across the whole brain with clusterwise correction; results are described by anatomical regions and statistical thresholds. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI acquisition parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related images and matched neutral images. It reports a within-subject contrast of smoking > neutral and conducts group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANCOVA) with cluster-level correction; results are reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex: women), cue type, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (Brain Voyager QX) are reported. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images vs matched objects). It reports within-participant contrasts (food>object) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results analyzed with mixed-effects FLAME and permutation-based whole-brain cluster correction (i.e., whole-brain voxelwise results are available). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing food cues to control objects (e.g., fattening food > object, non-fattening food > object, fattening > non-fattening). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using a region-of-interest voxelwise approach with cluster-thresholding corrections applied within anatomical masks (i.e., small-volume-corrected results) and coordinates/clusters are presented. Methods report participant age/sex (adult females), cue type (fattening vs non-fattening food images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FLAME). Full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only without small-volume correction, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue reactivity using pictorial alcohol stimuli in adolescents. The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts of alcoholic versus nonalcoholic pictures and voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical results (cluster-corrected), with coordinates/tables and figures (Tables 2–3, Figure 2). Participant demographics, cue type, scanning parameters, preprocessing, and software (AFNI) are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward conditioning using visual fractal cues predicting juice (natural reward) versus neutral outcomes. The study includes within-subject, task-evoked analyses of cue-related responses using temporal-difference model-based parametric regressors (value and RPE at cue onsets), and reports group-level voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates and t-values (ventral striatum, substantia nigra, amygdala), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain/SVC reporting. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8/FSL) are reported.
