Although the fMRI analyses are model-based parametric regressors rather than a simple categorical CS+>CS− contrast, these are within-participant cue-related voxelwise analyses indexing natural reward cue-reactivity and therefore meet the review’s requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (anticipatory shapes and words) to probe nondrug (monetary) reward cue-reactivity in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. It includes within-subject contrasts of reward cues > no-incentive cues (pre-response $1/$10 vs $0) and WIN vs HIT contrasts, and reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps with FDR-corrected results (whole-brain), with tables and figures. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, AFNI preprocessing/statistics) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cocaine vs neutral pictures (visual cues) in 23 cocaine-dependent participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of cocaine>neutral at the first level and group-level voxelwise second-level analyses with whole-brain, familywise-error-corrected results (tables/figures of coordinates and clusters provided). Methods include scanner field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and participant demographics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that directly includes a visual cue component (food image fMRI). It reports within-participant contrasts of [food images > non-food images] at the participant and group level, and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (one-sample and paired t-tests) with whole-brain analyses and ROI-based FWE correction; coordinate tables/figures and supplemental tables are provided. Participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual picture stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral control cues (alcohol vs. neutral picture contrast) and conducts group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (linear mixed-effects model in AFNI 3dLME) with cluster-wise multiple-comparisons correction (3dClustSim). Results are reported as voxelwise clusters/Z-scores and tabulated regions. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol pictures), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task fMRI study using visual smoking cues and within-subject contrasts (smoking images vs. neutral images) entered into analyses. Subject-level beta maps contrasting smoking vs. neutral images were derived and used in MVPA; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with cluster-wise family-wise error correction via wild bootstrapping) tested relationships between classification accuracy and behavioral attentional bias and group-by-bias interactions. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI, MVPA toolbox). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an event-related fMRI experiment of monetary reward expectation using visual instruction cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast: reward vs no-reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does NOT assess drug-related or natural reward-related cue-reactivity — it uses monetary/secondary rewards, which fall outside the meta-analysis target of drug or natural reward cues). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Therefore excluded for failing I3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (participant-selected food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (viewing food > viewing non-food; distraction food > distraction non-food) and carries out group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with family-wise error (FWE) cluster correction (p<0.05, cluster extent reported). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical fMRI task study that reports voxelwise, group-level task-evoked results (whole-brain thresholding and reported coordinates), includes within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation/outcome, and provides participant/sample and acquisition/preprocessing details, it does NOT investigate drug cues or natural reward-related cues. The task uses monetary incentives (monetary incentive delay), a secondary/extrinsic reward, rather than drug-related or natural reward cues (e.g., food, sexual, social). Therefore it fails the core content inclusion criteria I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue component) and I4 (within-participant drug>control or natural reward>control contrast as required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Because key inclusion criteria (I3 and I4) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (subliminal sexual images) with within-subject contrasts (Sex vs Neutral; Sex vs Fixation). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (Sex vs Neu: cluster-corrected results, Z>2.3, p<.05), and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the NAcc are also provided. Participant demographics and scanning/preprocessing details are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain and SVC results), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main results/tables), and I7 (participant and MRI details provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (highly palatable vs. moderately palatable, and moderate vs. neutral). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (explicitly states whole-brain analyses were conducted and reports cluster-corrected results and supporting information tables), and voxelwise results are available in Supporting Information. Participant demographics and cue types are reported; MRI acquisition and processing details are referenced in Supporting Information. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food image viewing). It contains within-participant contrasts (food vs non-food; high-calorie vs low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-level correction (voxelwise p<.001 with cluster extent thresholds derived from Monte Carlo simulations). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and participant and scanner details are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI task study using visual alcohol cues and neutral visual controls. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol-related cues > neutral cues) at the group level and presents voxelwise activation coordinates and T-values. Analysis used SPM8 with small-volume correction within a priori ROI masks (OFC, DLPFC, ACC, insula, amygdala) and reports SVC-corrected activations (coordinates, T values), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that included a clear visual cue component (visual labels during taste delivery), used a within-subject alcohol>water (alcohol vs. control) contrast, and reported whole-brain voxelwise group-level results with cluster correction and coordinate tables. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (white wine vs. water with visual labels), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using clear visual reward cues (coins for monetary, face images for social rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward>no reward for both anticipation and feedback. Group-level voxelwise analyses are presented (whole-brain thresholding and anatomical small-volume correction in a priori regions) with MNI coordinates and SPM results reported. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical software are provided. Although the study population focuses on ASD rather than substance use, the meta-analysis objective includes natural reward-related cue-reactivity; monetary and social rewards constitute natural/secondary reward cues and the study therefore provides qualifying cue>control voxelwise results. Full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of monetary reward anticipation using clear visual cues (coins), testing within-subject contrasts (e.g., €1.00 > €0.05). The paper reports group-level voxelwise results: whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected activations and ROI small-volume FWE-corrected striatal results, with MNI coordinates and statistics. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue contrasts). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-subject contrasts of food images versus neutral images. The paper reports voxel-wise multiple regression analyses and exploratory voxel-wise group contrasts with cluster coordinates and regional results (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), and provides key methodological details (participant demographics, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing software AFNI, statistical approach). Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity studies (food cues>neutral) and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual cues that predict cigarette (drug) and monetary (nondrug) reward, with trial-by-trial within-participant contrasts of reward-predicting cues (parametric increase in reward level, including a 0/no-reward level). Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (flexible factorial) are reported, with whole-brain thresholds and at least one FWE-corrected threshold; coordinates and cluster statistics are provided in the text (and supplementary). The methods explicitly describe visual cue presentation, 3T MRI acquisition, and use of SPM5 for preprocessing/statistics. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study investigates neural responses to natural reward (food) cues with a clear visual component (food pictures) and gustatory stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (food>nonfood, high-calorie>nonfood, chocolate>tasteless). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are presented with small-volume FWE-corrected statistics (cluster sizes, t values, P-FWE) in predefined ROIs; results are reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, contains within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This study does not meet the review’s core scope (drug or natural reward cue-reactivity). Although it is an fMRI task with visual cues and voxelwise, FWE-corrected cluster results within an ROI, the task used monetary (secondary) rewards rather than drug or natural rewards (e.g., food) and therefore fails to satisfy the primary inclusion criterion I3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with FWE correction / small-volume ROI), I6 (results availability indicated in text/tables/figures), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual cue component). I4 is not applicable because the within-participant contrast is monetary reward>baseline, not drug or natural reward cues>control. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., not ROI-only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs of appetizing, disgusting, bland foods and nonfood objects). It includes within-participant contrasts of appetizing>bland and appetizing>nonfood (cue>control) and reports group-level voxelwise statistical results with coordinate peaks and small-volume-corrected (SVC) results for a priori ROIs. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), participant age/sex, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (visual-only plus a small taste cue) comparing non–treatment-seeking alcoholic subjects and matched social drinkers. It reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > nonalcohol beverage cues and other cue>control contrasts, and performs group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM/MEDx) with cluster thresholds and reports activated clusters/tables (Table 2 and figures). The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (MEDx, SPM99). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward (food) cues and includes within-participant contrasts of hedonic food cues > nonfood objects. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (SPM8 random-effects, cluster-corrected threshold with MNI coordinates and tables/figures). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual smoking cues and matched visual control cues (I3). It includes a within-subject contrast of smoking>control cues (I4) and reports group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (one-sample and two-sample t tests) with coordinates/tables and figures (I5, I6). The authors used an a priori anatomical mask (WFU PickAtlas) to restrict voxelwise analyses to cue-related regions (i.e., a small-volume voxelwise approach) and report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing, and SPM2 software as well as participant demographics (I7). Results are reported as voxelwise task-evoked activations (tables/figures) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Although the sample is small (n=15) and the mask-based thresholding used an uncorrected p-value, the paper nonetheless provides group-level voxelwise task results suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity studies.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual food images (natural rewards). It includes a within-participant task-evoked contrast involving food cues versus baseline (described as “appetizing vs. plain > baseline”) at first level, reports group-level whole-brain corrected voxelwise results (FWE within-group, FDR between-groups) with cluster coordinates, and provides MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol advertisements as cues in a cue-reactivity paradigm in college students. It reports within-participant contrasts (ALCOHOL > CONTROL) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with cluster correction and peak MNI coordinates (Table 1 and whole-brain maps). Methods detail participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and statistical correction procedures. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I3–I7). No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not solely between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes (fulltext_incomplete = false).

This is an event-related fMRI study of a natural reward (erotic images) with explicit visual cues (X, O, ?). It reports within-participant contrasts for cues (X>O, ?>O) and for outcomes (erotic>neutral), and conducts group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses with FWE cluster correction and reported peak coordinates. Scanner field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM8), participant demographics (N, age, sex), and cue details are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug-related (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual photographic cues. It includes within-participant contrasts (smoking cues > neutral cues) at the group level, with voxelwise random-effects analyses reported (tables of coordinates, figures) using whole-brain thresholding (p<0.005, cluster extent) and SPM5 preprocessing. MRI field strength (3.0 T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it uses individualized script-driven imagery (auditory/internal imagery) rather than a visual cue component required by the meta-analysis. It does meet I4 (within-participant alcohol cue > neutral contrasts were analyzed), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported with whole-brain correction), I6 (voxelwise results and coordinates/figures/tables available), and I7 (participant demographics and methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (MA-related and pornographic images). It includes within-participant contrasts (MA vs. neutral; sex vs. neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with family-wise error correction (p<0.05). The manuscript provides participant demographics (male, 18–45), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-subject contrasts (high-energy vs. neutral; low-energy vs. neutral; high vs. low). Group-level voxelwise analyses were reported using whole-brain FDR correction (P<0.05) and cluster-level results; imaging acquisition (3T), preprocessing (DPARSF) and analysis software (SPM12) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI visual cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity that includes visual stimuli and reports qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results at the group level. Evidence: (1) Visual cues (pictures of alcohol) were presented (multimodal design including visual cues). (2) Within-participant contrasts (alcohol pictures vs control pictures and the opposites) were modeled and examined. (3) Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (mixed-effects), with results converted to Z-scores and cluster-wise FWE correction reported (cluster-wide p<0.05 FWE over the whole brain), satisfying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected reporting. (4) Required methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software FSL). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of e-cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (images of the e-cigarettes) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing conditioned (sweet-, nicotine-, sweet+nicotine-paired) cues to control/unexposed cues. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (p SVC values for NAcc) and whole-brain corrected correlations, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue types (sight and smell of e-cigarettes), MRI field strength (Siemens 3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), meeting reporting expectations. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related and neutral images (visual cue component) with within-participant contrasts (heroin-related > neutral). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses, p < .0001, cluster-level corrected) with coordinates in tables/figures. Methods report participant demographics (14 males, mean age), 3-T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), satisfying reporting preferences. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking-related images in 30 chronic smokers. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (aversive smoking-related vs. neutral; appetitive smoking-related vs. neutral) and reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and coordinate results (main text/supplementary tables). Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues and within-subject smoking cue>neutral contrasts (meets I3 and I4). Results include voxelwise group-level activations reported as coordinates in the main text (meets I6), and participant/MRI details and preprocessing software are reported (meets I7). However, all voxelwise analyses were conducted only within an ROI mask and statistical thresholds are reported as uncorrected (k=20, p<0.001) with no small-volume correction or whole-brain corrected results. Therefore the study does not provide a qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result (I5 not met) and falls under exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI-restricted results with no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug (methamphetamine) and natural reward (sexual) images with within-subject contrasts (methamphetamine>neutral; sexual>neutral) and group comparisons. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (cluster in left superior frontal cortex with peak coordinates, cluster size, and p-value using cluster-level FWE correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of high- and low-calorie foods and neutral non-foods). It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > non-food, and reports whole-brain voxel-wise group-level analyses (FWE- and FDR-corrected voxel-wise results) with MNI coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 and processing scripts), and participant age/sex/cue details. Results include voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the paper meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual cue-reactivity using e-cigarette advertising images (visual stimuli) presented to adolescents. It includes within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette cues > matched neutral control images and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected using AFNI 3dClustSim; results presented in tables and figures). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

The study uses the Monetary Incentive Delay Task with explicit reward versus neutral cues (visual cue onset modeled), providing within-participant reward>neutral contrasts (MID reward-neutral). It reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain mixed ANOVAs, FWE-corrected voxelwise results and whole-brain activation maps) and ROI analyses. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant reward>neutral contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in main text/figures), and I7 (participant characteristics and task/methods reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual reward cues (monetary and erotic) and an incentive delay task. The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (monetary > erotic) with cluster-wise FWE correction and reports small-volume-corrected voxelwise correlations between basal cortisol and the monetary-versus-erotic contrast in the ventral striatum. Reward and control conditions were explicitly modeled (reward cue vs control cue contrasts were computed, though not significant for the cortisol correlations). Participant details, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM2) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (pornography/erotic) cue-reactivity using visual cues and an event-related incentive delay task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing erotic cue conditions to control/other cue types and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results within a priori ventral striatum ROIs that survived small-volume FWE correction (PSVC-FWE<0.05). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and analysis tools (MATLAB, MarsBaR, WFU PickAtlas, SPSS mentioned) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the study does not rely solely on ROI-only uncorrected analyses, nor only connectivity/resting-state, nor lacks within-subject cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a within-participant task-evoked contrast of a natural reward cue (monetary) versus control (50¢>0¢). The monetary cue was presented visually (money reminder cue and word stimuli), satisfying the visual-cue requirement. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with voxel-wise thresholds, cluster extent correction, and coordinates for significant clusters, and provides sufficient methodological details (participants’ age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Although drug-word versus neutral-word contrasts were collapsed and not emphasized, the monetary 50¢>0¢ within-subject contrast qualifies as a natural reward-related cue>control contrast. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards.

This task-based fMRI study used visually presented word cues (alcohol- and cannabis-related words) in an addiction-Stroop task, including within-participant contrasts of alcohol>neutral (color) and cannabis>neutral. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed with SPM8 and cluster-level correction (3dClustSim) and report significant clusters and correlations, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, first- and second-level analyses), results, and discussion; key details (participant demographics, cue type, 3T field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and whole-brain corrected voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-participant contrasts) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues vs neutral images with within-participant contrasts (heroin-related > neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses reported using SPM5. Results are reported at p≤0.05 FWE-corrected with cluster threshold and regional activations are described. Participant demographics (male, age range), MRI field strength (1.5 T), cue type (visual heroin-related images), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts, but all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (average timecourses from a priori spheres) rather than group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise result (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual smoking-related and affective images and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral, positive>neutral, negative>neutral) entered into random-effects group analyses. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (interaction in left middle frontal gyrus with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected significance), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result. Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T field strength, SPM8 preprocessing). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation using visual food images (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (appetizing > non-foods and appetizing > bland) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction in striatal ROIs. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/software (SPM5), and participant details are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and provides qualifying small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual drug-word stimuli (words presented visually) and a rewarded drug cue-reactivity task. The paper reports within-subject condition contrasts across drug vs neutral word conditions (2×2 ANOVA with word and money factors and condition-specific ROI comparisons, e.g., neutral vs drug at 0¢ and drug at 50¢ conditions) and condition-specific whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain, cluster-level corrected group-level voxelwise results are reported (Table 1; cluster-level corrected P < 0.001), and voxelwise regression/contrast analyses (small-volume corrected ROI regressions) are presented. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for visual cue component, within-participant contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (greyscale landscape photographs) to probe anticipation of monetary reward and punishment. It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts of reward-predicting > neutral cues and punishment-predicting > neutral cues at the group level, with SPM5 preprocessing and statistical analysis. Results report small-volume-corrected (SVC) voxelwise activations (FWE-corrected spherical search volumes) in a priori regions and report coordinates/activations in the main text/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity to natural (monetary) rewards with visual stimuli and provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (milkshake vs water images). It includes within-participant contrasts of milkshake cue > tasteless-solution cue and milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt, and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses corrected for multiple comparisons with coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12; AFNI for cluster correction) and many methodological details are provided in the full text. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity and voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay task with visual cues signaling gain vs nongain (within-participant contrasts of reward>control). Group-level voxelwise results are reported including small-volume-corrected (SVC) ROI analyses (pFWE<.05) and whole-brain FWE-corrected results for key contrasts. Participant demographics and scanning/method details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This study uses BOLD-fMRI with clear visual natural-reward cues (erotic video) and reports within-subject contrasts (sexual stimulation vs neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses. Methods state preprocessing with SPM99, smoothing, voxelwise activation maps with cluster and t-threshold (p<0.01), and independent two-sample t-tests comparing groups, with figures showing whole-brain activation patterns. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and software are reported. The design therefore meets I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results presented in figures/tables), and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures) and within-participant contrasts (food vs. non-food; high-calorie vs. non-food). Group-level voxelwise results are reported and corrected using small-volume correction (FWE-corrected voxel-level results within a priori ROIs) and whole-brain thresholds for non-ROI regions. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant demographics and cue types. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

The study uses an fMRI monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual cues signaling reward, providing a natural reward-related visual cue component. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., anticipation of reward > anticipation of no outcome) and group-level voxelwise statistical results (voxelwise FWE-corrected activations and small-volume correction reported; coordinates provided). Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/ connectivity-only, and includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (Food-pics images) that examines neural responses to natural reward-related stimuli. It includes within-subject task regressors for food trials (go and no-go trials modeled) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (3dMVM exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates and cluster tables). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, ANTs, SPM not needed) are reported. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, contains within-participant cue-related contrasts, and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates.

This is an fMRI task study of natural reward (food) using visual cues with within-participant contrasts (HC-NF, LC-NF) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses constrained to a priori striatal ROI with reported coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I6 (voxelwise results reported as coordinates), I7 (reports participant characteristics, cue types, 3T field strength, SPM8 preprocessing). However, the qualifying group-level voxelwise result was presented only within ROI masks and statistical thresholding was reported as uncorrected (P<0.05, cluster ≥5 voxels) with no small-volume correction or whole-brain corrected results provided. Therefore it does not meet I5 (requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise evidence) and meets exclusion E3 (only ROI analyses without qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the monetary incentive delay task with clear visual cues (geometric symbols) to probe reward anticipation (a natural reward). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of gain anticipation versus neutral (¥20+¥100+¥500 > ¥0), and group-level voxelwise results using whole-brain thresholds and an a priori NAc ROI with FWE small-volume correction. Coordinates, tables, and figures of activation are reported. Participant demographics (n=19, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/MATLAB) are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- vs low-caloric food images). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-caloric > low-caloric) and group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for visual cue-based task-evoked voxelwise analyses and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures and emotional faces). It includes within-participant contrasts (alcpic > con, pospic > con, negpic > con) and reports group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain cluster correction (pcorrected < 0.05 using 3dClustSim) and tables of significant clusters/coordinates. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and participant demographics are reported. Thus the paper provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise (whole-brain-corrected) analyses of visual drug-related cues vs. control. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This empirical fMRI study examines food (a natural reward) cue-related anticipation and receipt using visual cues (abstract snack/ basket and wallet images) and directly contrasts high vs no reward within participants (10 SP vs 0 SP; EUR1 vs 0). Group-level voxelwise results are reported both as small-volume-corrected ROI findings (FWE-corrected) and whole-brain cluster-corrected results. Relevant methodological details (participant age ranges, sex matching, cue types, 3T scanner, preprocessing and SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (hardcore sexual penetration images) and reports within-participant contrasts (PEN > NEU). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and small-volume-corrected analyses; coordinate tables and figures are provided. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T Philips), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol images (visual stimuli) and a within-participant alcohol>neutral beverage contrast. The paper reports group-level voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses within a striatum mask (masked voxelwise thresholding with cluster-level correction and MNI coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise result (small-volume-corrected). Relevant details (participant sex, cue type, 3T scanner, SPM5 preprocessing) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs. neutral/abstract) at first-level and group-level voxelwise analyses reported (whole-brain linear correlations with coordinates and cluster sizes). The methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and SPM5 analysis, and participant demographics (age/sex). Voxelwise group results (p-values, coordinates, clusters) are presented in the main text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for within-participant cue>control contrasts, task-evoked voxelwise group results, and reporting details required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (appetizing vs. bland food pictures) with an explicit within-participant contrast (appetizing > bland foods). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses and small-volume-corrected PET/SVC results), provides coordinates and statistical thresholds, and details MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related pictures). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking vs. neutral pictures (cue>control) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (2×2 ANOVA and planned t-tests) with FWE-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables. Voxelwise results are provided in tables/figures and described in the text. Core content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text; supplementary details are noted but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked fMRI data are reported). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual food cues (food vs nonfood images) and reports within-participant task contrasts (food>nonfood) across timepoints. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (flexible factorial and two-sample t tests, voxelwise thresholds, cluster statistics, tables/figures), and small-volume/ROI analyses for the hypothalamus are also provided. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (visual food images), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), satisfying reporting preferences. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes task-evoked voxelwise results; includes within-participant contrasts; is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using audiovisual (visual) stimuli, scanned at 3.0T. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking control cues and presents group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses with whole-brain voxelwise results reported as coordinates and tables/figures (MNI coordinates, t-values). Methods include participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, ASLtbx). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts). Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual sexual stimuli (sexual vs. neutral). The design includes within-participant contrasts (sexual>neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results within a mesolimbic mask and whole-brain cluster-corrected results. Participant details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, MATLAB) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-participant contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This paper is a task-based fMRI study using visual heroin-related pictorial cues and neutral control images (I3). Analyses include a within-participant contrast (heroin-related > neutral) used at the group level (I4). Higher-level group analyses were performed voxelwise with FSL FLAME and results thresholded using whole-brain cluster correction (z>2, cluster p<0.05), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (I5). Results are reported in the text and figures (with coordinates/tables referenced), meeting I6. Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing, and software (FSL/FEAT), so I7 is met (preferred metadata present). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study using visual natural reward cues (erotic pictures) and monetary cues in a within-subject design. It includes within-participant contrasts of high>low erotic cues (reward-related cues) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume-corrected statistics in predefined ROIs (ventral striatum, amygdala, OFC, hypothalamus) with t-values/p-values and coordinates described. Results and methods (participants’ age/sex, 3T MRI field, preprocessing with SPM12/DARTEL/CAT12) are reported. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue contrasts, and qualifying voxelwise (small-volume-corrected) group results. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

Exclusion decision because the study does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward cues versus a control stimulus (e.g., appetizing food > unappetizing food or food images > neutral) required by I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual food images), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain results with cluster correction reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables), I7 (participant age/sex and MRI details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no qualifying within-participant natural reward-related cues>control-stimuli contrast presented; the reported contrasts compare reappraisal instructions while viewing appetizing foods rather than food cues versus non-food/neutral control). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in nicotine-dependent humans using visual smoking-related cues vs matched neutral images (meets I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral during encoding and retrieval (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain cluster correction (Z=2.3, p<0.05) and reported coordinates/tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (FSL) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E4), and include within-subject cue>control contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E5). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This article is an fMRI cue-reactivity study that includes visual cue components (multimodal tactile+visual cues) and reports within-subject cue contrasts (primary contrast MJ cue > fruit cue). Group-level voxelwise results are reported via whole-brain PLSC-derived voxel clusters with bootstrap ratios and supplemental cluster tables. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT; R/TExPosition), participant ages, cue types, and task details are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-based fMRI cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol-related versus neutral stimuli (main effect of condition and the planned contrast isolating alcohol-related inhibition [(NoGo_alcohol > Go_alcohol) > (NoGo_neutral > Go_neutral)]). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain thresholding and small-volume FWE correction; MNI coordinates and cluster details are provided. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12), and participant demographics are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group contrasts without within-participant cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (visual photographs) and multimodal (visual + auditory) design. The study reports within-participant contrasts of high-energy-dense (high-ED) > low-ED food cues for visual and auditory modalities (e.g., fed visual high-ED > fed visual low-ED), satisfying the cue>control contrast requirement. Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with whole-brain thresholding, cluster correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and reported supra-threshold clusters/coordinates, meeting the whole-brain voxelwise evidence requirement. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures) as natural reward stimuli. The study reports within-subject contrasts of food>scenery (food minus scenery) and presents group-level voxelwise t-maps with coordinates and multiple-comparisons-corrected peaks (whole-brain results). Scanner field strength, participant age/sex, cue types, preprocessing, and statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cues with visual stimuli and reports seed-based PPI task-dependent connectivity results (VTA connectivity changes) but does not present a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast (high-calorie cue > control) at the group level within this manuscript. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without also reporting a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cue paradigm) and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control activation contrast reported in this full text) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation result/whole-brain or SVC reported here). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines neural responses to sexual cues and sexual stimuli (natural rewards) using visual cues (text announcements) and visual stimuli (pictures/videos). It reports within-participant contrasts CUE SEM > CUE NEUTRAL and SEM > NEUTRAL. Results include small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (FWE SVC) and explorative whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine images (visual-only cues) in male cocaine users and controls. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine cues > neutral/control cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE-corrected) as well as small-volume-corrected ROI results for the amygdala and ventral striatum. Methods report MRI field strength, preprocessing and SPM8 analysis details, and participant demographics. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying voxelwise group-level results.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). It includes within-participant first-level contrasts (food > objects and high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports second-level random-effects group analyses. Voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (ROI SVC, FWE-corrected) meeting the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Relevant methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, 3T MRI, SPM8 preprocessing/statistics). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and figures/tables of voxelwise results are described. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI/no voxelwise results; only connectivity; only between-group contrasts; non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study used an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity paradigm with visual alcohol vs non-alcohol beverage images and reports group-level effects based on extracted percent signal change from an a priori right ventral striatum sphere (ROI) and subsequent GLM analyses. However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain results or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (no coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps/SVC reported). Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result (E3) and does not meet the required inclusion criterion for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant ALC>BEV contrast), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise coordinates/figures/tables provided). Full text is complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given E3 is met, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual cue-based monetary reward anticipation task (arrow cues) and reports within-participant contrasts (anticipation of monetary reward > anticipation of verbal feedback). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain analyses with coordinates and ROI-corrected VS results), and necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets the review objective of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking>neutral) and a group-level whole-brain 2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA with FWE-corrected results; peak activations are listed in tables/figures (coordinates available). Methods report participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). The paper therefore meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (task-evoked voxelwise results are present alongside connectivity analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural reward) and directly contrasts food > non-food within participants. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (random-effects ‘food > non-food’ contrasts) and several clusters were confirmed with small-volume/ROI correction (p < .005). The paper provides necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing with SPM99) and presents whole-brain and ROI-corrected voxelwise results in the main text. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as a natural reward (food) cue-reactivity fMRI study with visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cues (natural rewards) that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (high-ED > low-ED; large PS > small PS) and provides sufficient methodological detail (age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). However, the article explicitly states that data for the nonfood control conditions (scrambled images and furniture) were not presented, and no within-participant contrast of cue > control (food > nonfood) is reported. Inclusion criterion I4 requires at least one within-participant cue>control contrast; that criterion is not satisfied here. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (no reported cue>control within-participant analysis).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli tailored to participants’ drug of dependence. Methods report within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues at the first level and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with whole-brain cluster correction (coordinates and clusters reported). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, AFNI’s 3dClustSim) and participant demographics are provided. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The study includes within-participant contrasts of food>non-food at first level, and group-level voxelwise inference using FSL RANDOMISE (TFCE, FWE-corrected) within predefined masks (small-volume approach), with cluster peaks and MNI coordinates reported. Participant age range, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT, ICA-AROMA, RANDOMISE) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The paradigm used visual food and animal images and reports within-participant contrasts (food > animal/blurred baseline). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA with FDR correction) and clusters/coordinates are reported for ROIs (left/right middle frontal gyrus). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (HiCal>Control, LoCal>Control, Food>Control) and group-level voxelwise results using SPM8 with small-volume correction (ROI mask) and MNI coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food images (high- and low-calorie) as natural reward cues and non-food control images, with within-participant contrasts (e.g., high-calorie > non-food; high > low). Results are reported as whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise statistical maps with Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholds (group-level task-evoked voxelwise results). Methods describe MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-based natural reward fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photo pairs of high- and low-calorie foods and objects). The study reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > object, low-calorie > object, food > object) and performs group-level voxelwise random-effects GLM analyses with cluster-based multiple-comparison correction (family-wise p < .05) and reports coordinates/cluster results. Results are presented for pre- and postmeal states, and voxelwise group comparisons are reported. Therefore the paper satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without cue>control, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual smoking images (ISIS) versus matched neutral pictures (I3). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral stimuli (block design) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (one-sample, two-sample, and paired t-tests) with coordinates, cluster sizes, and corrected cluster thresholds (satisfying I4–I6). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics via SPM5), meeting I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E4), and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E5). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary cues (pink cross/green circle predicting 75¢ vs 0¢) and reports within-participant contrasts of Cue Money > No-money (Cue Money – No-money) and Receive Money – No-money. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with multiple-comparison correction) and ROI small-volume-corrected voxelwise results, i.e., group-level task-evoked voxelwise statistical findings. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, preprocessing, and statistical approach. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (audiovisual heroin and matched neutral images). It reports within-subject contrasts of heroin vs neutral conditions and a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise 2×2 ANOVA with cluster correction (z>=3.1, cluster p<=0.05), providing task-evoked voxelwise results (clusters and coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is included.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of anticipation of monetary and verbal rewards using clear visual cues (distinct CS arrows). It includes within-participant voxelwise group-level contrasts comparing reward-predicting cues to control cues (mCS+ > CS−, vCS+ > CS−, mCS+ > vCS+) analyzed with second-level random-effects and reports whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (Gaussian random field theory, P < 0.05 corrected). Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay task with explicit visual cues (circle vs square) signaling reward vs neutral trials (natural monetary reward), and includes within-participant contrasts of reward>neutral (anticipation) as well as group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (p<0.05 corrected). The paper also reports a small-volume ROI analysis of the nucleus accumbens. Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), and participant demographics are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of cocaine, neutral objects, blurred controls). The within-participant Cocaine>Object contrast was explicitly computed and used in ROI and group analyses. The paper also reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise Cocaine>Object activation maps (cluster-corrected p=0.05) in the Supplementary Whole-brain fMRI Analysis, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T Siemens Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation using visual food cues (natural rewards) with whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (cluster-wise correction) and reports coordinates/figures, but it does not present a within-participant contrast of reward cues versus control/neutral stimuli (e.g., food cue > neutral/baseline). The reported main contrasts are HE (high-energy) versus LE (low-energy) food choices and SL versus DL liking conditions, which compare two types of reward cues to each other rather than reward cues to a neutral control. Because inclusion criterion I4 requires at least one within-participant cue>control contrast, this study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study using visual cue videos (cocaine, gambling, sad) that elicited cue-specific cravings/urges. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing video epochs to baseline (V1>B1, V2>B2) and reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (3×2×3 ANOVAs) with whole-brain family-wise-error correction (Monte Carlo simulation). Neuroimaging results are presented in tables and figures (Table 2, Figures, Supplementary Figures), satisfying reporting requirements. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objectives and inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise corrected results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (500-ms images) in cocaine-dependent participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of cocaine > neutral (first and second halves) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, with ROI-based cluster correction and whole-brain cluster-corrected results (coordinates/tables/figures provided). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8, ASLtbx), and statistical software (GLM Flex Fast 2, AFNI cluster correction), and participant demographics (age, sex). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol images) and non-alcohol control images in young adult college students. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverages and repetition effects (second vs first presentation). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses are reported with cluster-level correction (cluster extent threshold 8127 μl, p<.05) and results presented in tables/figures (coordinates and clusters in Table 3 and 4, Figures 2–5). Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical BOLD-fMRI study of smokers using visual smoking cues (pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing smoking versus neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain results and coordinates, e.g., dACC coordinates and Z values) and whole-brain correlation analyses. MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), participant age/sex, and cue type are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Inclusion justified for meta-analysis of visual drug-cue reactivity.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic video stimuli (natural reward) with a within-subject erotic>non-erotic contrast at the group level.
