The paper reports whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and provides MNI coordinates and cluster sizes (qualifying voxelwise results). Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, empirical task-evoked fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the paper reports only ROI-based analyses and uses extracted parameter estimates rather than presenting any group-level voxelwise, whole-brain, or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (meets exclusion criterion E3). Included criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images), I4 (within-participant Food > Non-Food contrast was computed), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and software are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the manuscript does not report at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise result (whole-brain or SVC-corrected) or coordinate table/figure showing such task-evoked activations for Food>Control. Therefore it must be excluded per the review criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food and nonfood images). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie food; food > nonfood) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction (FWE-corrected ROI mask) showing significant activation differences (right putamen/pallidum). Results are reported in the main text and figures; participant demographics and preprocessing software (SPM5) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. MRI field strength is not explicitly stated in the provided text, but this omission alone does not preclude inclusion per protocol. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for voxelwise cue-reactivity analyses with visual stimuli.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue reactivity in children. The fMRI task used visual food images (high-ED and low-ED; plus furniture/scrambled images), and group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results with peak coordinates and cluster size). A within-participant contrast was reported (high-ED > low-ED food images), which constitutes a cue-related contrast of differing reward stimuli. Whole-brain voxelwise results are provided and corrected for multiple comparisons. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug (tobacco) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images. It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral images and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM and mixed-effects ANCOVA) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level correction (p<0.05). Results are reported in the text and tables/figures. Participant characteristics (adult women), cue type (visual smoking images), MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX and preprocessing steps) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes qualifying within-subject contrast). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). The study includes within-participant contrasts (unhealthy foods > healthy foods and vice versa). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses were performed and reported with whole-brain cluster correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and results described in the main text (with ROI analyses also reported). The manuscript provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Methods report within-participant contrasts (sexual vs neutral; sexual vs other rewards) and group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain and region-of-interest small-volume analyses) with coordinates and figures (supplementary tables referenced). MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, MarsBar) are reported; participant characteristics are provided. All required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity in human participants using visual cues paired with tastes. It includes within-participant cue contrasts (anticipatory palatable cue > sub-palatable cue; matched palatable > matched sub-palatable; prediction error contrasts), satisfying I4. The study used whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (FSL Randomise with TFCE, reported coordinates and cluster-level FWE p-values), satisfying I5 and I6. The design includes a clear visual cue component (taste-paired cues), satisfying I3. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete=true). It is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, nor non-empirical, and contains qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results, so no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity studies using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of adolescent alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol-picture stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > non-alcohol beverage cues, and group-level voxelwise analyses (AFNI 3dttest++ whole-brain exploratory analysis and ROI cluster-corrected results using AlphaSim) with reported significant clusters (locations, cluster sizes, corrected p-values). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, lack of within-subject cue>control contrast, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked cue-reactivity with visual stimuli.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (images of alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) with a within-participant contrast (alcoholic>non-alcoholic) reported at the group level as voxelwise results (one-sample t-test, voxel-level analysis with reported coordinates/regions). The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise activation results (coordinates, figures/tables), details of MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics. Full methods, results, and discussion are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity that includes visual cue exposure (participants held a cigarette and a live video feed of their hand was shown), and reports within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette cue > control cue. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (main effect of cue and interaction effects) with coordinates and cluster thresholds (AFNI/AlphaSim), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL, etc.). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The full text describes a human pCASL perfusion fMRI study using visual smoking-cue (video) and non-smoking control video, with within-subject SCs > non-SCs contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were conducted using an anatomically defined ROI mask with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-based correction (i.e., small-volume-corrected results) and coordinates are reported in Table 2. Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using clearly visual food-video stimuli. The study includes within-participant contrasts of food video (FV) > control video epochs and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results using SPM2 with family-wise error correction (voxel-level FWE P<0.05) and cluster reporting; coordinates are referenced (Table 2). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues/feedback (symbolic cues and visual feedback images of wallets and faces) and includes within-participant contrasts comparing reward-related stimuli to a neutral “no outcome” baseline (e.g., anticipation: anticipation hit outcome > anticipation no outcome; consumption: consumption hit outcome > consumption no outcome). Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise SPM5 whole-brain procedures with reported peak coordinates (and supplementary data). Participant demographics, cue types, field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. These features satisfy all inclusion criteria for task-evoked, visual cue-related reward reactivity. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual erotic vs. neutral pictures. It includes within-subject contrasts (placebo/erotic > placebo/neutral; GHB/neutral > placebo/neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (threshold p<.001, k>15) as well as small-volume (FWE) corrected ROI results with coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cigarette-related stimuli (FDA graphic vs non-graphic warning labels) and measures cue-evoked craving. It includes within-participant contrasts (graphic > non-graphic and graphic > baseline), reports group-level voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster-level correction, and conducts a priori ROI (small-volume) analyses with corrected statistics. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/software (FSL), and participant age/sex. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol-related images (IAPS) with a within-participant contrast (alcohol>neutral). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: whole-brain analyses (peak-level p<.001, cluster-level FWE p<.05) and anatomically defined small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the bilateral amygdala (FWE-corrected p<.05). Participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is a human task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward). It includes a within-participant contrast (high-calorie > low-calorie foods). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction in the hypothalamus (one voxel survives SVC, coordinate and p=0.0125), and results are described in text and figures. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie food pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > control (cars) and performs group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with cluster- and voxel-level correction and reported coordinates), satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The meta-analysis requires studies with a clear visual cue component (I3). This study used multimodal cue induction consisting of auditory scripts and olfactory cues (smell of participants’ favorite alcohol and orange juice) but no visual cues are described, so it fails I3. The full text is complete. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: within-participant cue contrasts (A>N) were performed (I4); group-level voxelwise task-evoked results were reported via ROI-based second-level analyses with small-volume/ROI correction and voxel coordinates (I5, I6); and participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM5) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore EXCLUDED solely because it does not meet I3 (no visual cue component).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). First-level within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > neutral/control were computed. Group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise LME) were reported with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values for significant voxels (DLPFC, MTL, VLPFC), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Necessary methodological details are provided (participant sex counts, age covariate, cue type, MRI field strengths 1.5T and 3T, preprocessing with SPM12), and coordinate results are reported in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking and neutral images, with within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (group mPFC cluster with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected p-value) and individual voxelwise hot-spot coordinates; results are presented with coordinates and statistical thresholds. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM5), and participant age/sex are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual cues (images of milkshake vs water) signaling impending milkshake delivery. It reports within-participant contrasts (milkshake cue > tasteless solution cue; milkshake receipt > tasteless solution receipt). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster-corrected via Monte Carlo simulations) with coordinates in tables and figures; ROI analyses with voxel-wise FWE correction are also reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL, AFNI modules) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcoholic beverage) at the individual level and group-level voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates and tables; some results were tested with family-wise error correction and voxelwise analyses are reported (voxel-wise threshold and cluster extent provided). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI), participant demographics (age- and gender-matched groups), and cue types. Full article includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This full-text reports an empirical 1.5T fMRI study using visual alcohol-drinking video cues and a mosaic control, with within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs mosaic) and group-level voxelwise GLM/RFX results (clusters reported with FDR correction and tabulated coordinates). Methods include MRI field strength, preprocessing, and analysis software (BrainVoyager), and participant demographics are described. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). The study reports within-participant contrasts of food cues > control (Food vs Objects; Unhealthy Food vs Objects; Healthy Food vs Objects) at the group level, and reports voxelwise group-level results including whole-brain cluster-corrected activations and ROI analyses. Voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results are described and thresholding/correction methods reported. Participant demographics and cue types are reported; some methodological details (e.g., scanner field strength) are not explicit but this alone does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an fMRI task study using visual infant face stimuli (baby schema) as natural reward-related cues in opioid-dependent participants. It includes within-subject contrasts (Low, Unmanipulated, High baby schema; modeled vs crosshair and comparisons across levels) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (FEAT/FSL whole-brain analyses, cluster-corrected at z=3.1, p<0.005 FWE) with activation in the ventral striatum. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT), participant demographics, and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity that includes visual (and tactile) cue presentations. It reports within-participant contrasts (cannabis>neutral, cannabis>fruit, fruit>neutral) and group-level voxelwise results using mixed-effects FLAME with cluster-level FWE correction (whole-brain voxelwise results reported). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, FSL/FEAT/FLAME), and cue types are described. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-evoked, voxelwise visual cue-reactivity are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study assesses natural reward-related cue-reactivity (social and monetary rewards) using clear visual cues (graphical monetary cues, wallet images, and pictures of smiling faces). Within-participant cue-related contrasts were modeled at cue onset (reward levels vs control), and group-level voxelwise results are reported: a whole-brain analysis (FWE-corrected) for main effects and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis (FWE) in the nucleus accumbens showing an interaction. Key methodological details (participant age/sex counts, cue types, MRI field strength = 1.5T, preprocessing/statistics using SPM5) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in children comparing obese and normal-weight responses to visual food cues. It includes within-subject contrasts (food > neutral), reports group-level voxelwise random-effects results with whole-brain and ROI-corrected statistics (coordinates/tables/figures), and provides necessary methodological details (participant demographics, cue type, 1.5T MRI, SPM5 preprocessing). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Exclusion basis: No qualifying within-participant visual cue > control contrast was reported. (a) Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 strictly apply. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study with clear visual cues: visual words 'Alcohol' and 'Water' presented), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported for taste/PE contrasts), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement), I7 (reported participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 was not satisfied — the paper does not report a within-participant contrast of visual drug cue > control cue (analyses and reported results focus on taste/outcome contrasts and prediction-error effects rather than cue>control visual cue contrasts). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the cue-reactivity meta-analysis and is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) cues versus neutral control photographs with within-subject contrasts (S > N) reported. The paper reports group-level voxelwise statistical results (SPM99; fixed-effects group analysis with whole-brain thresholds and coordinates) and individual voxelwise results for lower-brain analyses. Participant demographics (age, male sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-subject task-evoked contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. Methods state brain responses to food pictures were recorded and individual contrasts were computed (postprandial vs baseline), and associations between GLP-1 changes and food-cue responses were tested using SPM8 with whole-brain FWE correction (p<0.05), yielding voxelwise group-level results in the orbitofrontal cortex. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; includes within-participant cue-related contrasts). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity studies of natural rewards with visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity but the experimental cues are gustatory (taste delivery of alcohol vs juice) rather than visual, so it does not meet I3 (visual cue component). It does include a within-participant contrast Alcohol>Juice (I4 met) and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (I7 met). However, voxelwise results are limited: primary findings are ROI-based, and the exploratory whole-brain analysis reported only uncorrected clusters (no whole-brain FWE/FDR-corrected or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). Therefore it fails I5. Because the paper reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC-corrected result, exclusion criterion E3 applies. Inclusion met: I4, I7. Inclusion not met: I3, I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of stress-induced cocaine craving using personalized guided-imagery (audiotaped scripts) rather than visual drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria I3 (clear visual cue component) is not met because the paradigm used auditory guided imagery, not visual cue presentations. Inclusion criterion I4 (a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control) is not met: the within-subject contrasts are stress (imagery) vs neutral imagery or imagery vs baseline, not a drug-cue (visual) > control contrast. The full text does contain task-evoked, voxelwise whole-brain results, so I5 is satisfied; results are presented in figures/tables (I6) and participant/method details reported (I7). However, failure to meet I3 and I4 means the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective, so it must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcoholic > non-alcoholic beverages) and second-level group voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with small-volume (mesocorticolimbic mask) and FWE/FDR-corrected results (tables and figures). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core voxelwise task-evoked results are provided. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual picture stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol>neutral), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results using SPM with voxel p<.001 and cluster-level FWE correction, and provides coordinates and cluster descriptions. The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Note: some acquisition details (e.g., MRI field strength) appear referenced in supplementary material, but lack of that single detail does not preclude inclusion per the review’s guidance (I7 is preferred, not required).

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts (available > non-available food; high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: whole-brain t-tests and ROI analyses with small-volume FWE-corrected peaks (coordinates reported) for the availability contrast (e.g., ACC, OFC, caudate). Participants’ age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity studies using visual natural rewards.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of tobacco use disorder using visual smoking-related cues and neutral control pictures. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (tobacco-related > neutral) during cue-exposure and neurofeedback runs, with group-level voxelwise voxelwise t-tests, cluster thresholds and Bonferroni correction, and provides coordinates/figures. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (visual smoking pictures), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager/Turbo-BrainVoyager) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food [high+low] vs nonfood; high-calorie vs low-calorie; high-calorie vs nonfood). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported using whole-brain random-effects analyses with familywise error correction and ROI small-volume corrections (nucleus accumbens, insula, hypothalamus), with coordinates provided. Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3.0-T MRI field strength, SPM12 preprocessing/statistics). The full text supplied contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This full-text fMRI study uses visual cue stimuli (geometric cues in a monetary incentive delay task) probing natural reward (monetary) cue-reactivity and reports within-subject contrasts (gain > neutral; loss > neutral). Group-level voxelwise SPM5 analyses are reported with coordinate results and applied small-volume correction for ventral striatum (pFWE), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/SVC voxelwise results. Participant demographics, cue type, 1.5T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are documented. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue-reactivity.

Exclusion: E3 applies — the study reports only an ROI-based analysis (mean beta values from 5-mm spheres) and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results for the qualifying contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of a natural reward — food — with clear visual cue stimuli) and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli is reported in the paper’s results — contrasts reported are between portion-size/ED conditions rather than cue>control), and I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results are provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This fMRI study tests neural responses to social (natural) vs monetary rewards using visual cues (dynamic video clips). It includes within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control cues (e.g., social reward vs social control; monetary reward vs monetary control) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (main effects and contrasts) plus a small-volume-corrected ROI result in the nucleus accumbens (FWE-corrected). Coordinates and statistical maps/tables are reported. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing/analysis) are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (smoking vs neutral images) during a Go/NoGo task, addressing cue-reactivity. The authors conducted within-subject contrasts of smoking versus neutral images and performed group-level voxelwise analyses using FSL Randomise with an anatomically defined ROI mask (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). Results (including null voxelwise contrasts) and ROI-extracted beta weights are reported in text, figures, and tables. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI with qualifying voxelwise/small-volume-corrected analyses.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food > non-food images. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) and results are presented in figures and tables; preprocessing and analysis software (FSL/FEAT) and MRI field strength (3T) are described, and participant age/sex and cue type are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrast, empirical human fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cocaine cues vs neutral cues, reporting within-participant contrasts (cocaine cues > neutral cues) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain results. The methods specify visual stimuli, GLM first-level contrasts (cocaine cues vs neutral), and higher-level mixed-effects whole-brain analyses with cluster thresholding; tables/figures and coordinates are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains the qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full-text reports an fMRI task exposing participants to visual marketing clips (alcohol, cannabis, neutral) and includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol marketing > neutral; cannabis marketing > neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (with significant clusters and cluster-level FWE correction) and ROI/SVC analyses in striatum are described. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 statistical software, and participant demographics. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in main text/tables/figures), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual stimuli (visual HED vs LED food cues) and multimodal (visual + auditory) design. The study reports within-participant contrasts HED > LED (visual and auditory) and conducts whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster-extent correction, reporting peak coordinates and statistical findings. Methods (participants, imaging parameters, preprocessing, statistical models) and results are fully described in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (wine) cue effects where visual price cues were presented and manipulated. It includes a within-subject contrast of price cue conditions (high vs low) that tests cue-related effects on brain activation and experienced pleasantness. Voxelwise whole-brain multilevel mediation analyses are reported, and results were corrected using small-volume correction (SVC) for a priori ROIs; coordinates and voxelwise results are provided in tables/figures. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, Mediation Toolbox) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study examines visual food cue reactivity (natural reward) with within-subject food>control contrasts and reports voxelwise group results and coordinates, but it does NOT report any group-level voxelwise results that are whole-brain corrected or small-volume-corrected. The food>cars contrasts used to localize ROIs are reported at p<.05 uncorrected; therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant food>control contrasts), I6 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported), I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (effectively only ROI/connectivity-focused results without a qualifying corrected voxelwise task map). Full text appears complete for screening. Given the lack of qualifying corrected voxelwise results, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related visual cues (food images) with within-participant contrasts (hedonic foods > utilitarian foods; utilitarian foods > neutral objects). Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed (whole-brain analyses with FDR correction reported) and ROI analyses supplement these results. MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), participant age/sex, and cue types are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (pictorial cues) within a multimodal design (visual + auditory). It employed within-subject contrasts (high-ED and low-ED food cues vs. neutral nonfood cues and high-ED>low-ED comparisons) at the group level. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM5 and results are reported as statistical maps, figures, and a coordinate table (Table 1) with cluster-correction procedures described. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (random-effects), with whole-brain FDR-corrected results reported for several regions and a priori ROI thresholds described; coordinate results are indicated to be listed. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study examines visual food cues (natural reward) using an fMRI anticipatory task (square cue preceding food images vs object images). It includes within-participant contrasts (Food Anticipation > Object Anticipation and Food Image > Object Image) and conducts whole-brain voxelwise group- and within-subject analyses with voxel thresholds and cluster correction (AlphaSim). Key voxelwise results are reported with coordinates (e.g., right ventral anterior insula, xyz=38,11,-8) and cluster volumes in the main text. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes a within-subject first-level contrast of food stimuli > neutral stimuli that was entered into a group-level (second-level) voxelwise full-factorial analysis. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (thresholded at uncorrected P<0.001, k>5) with stereotactic coordinates provided. Participant demographics (female, age 20–30), cue type (individualized food images), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Magnetom), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images (ISIS). The design includes within-participant contrasts (delay conditions: smoking cues vs control/neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise GLM results with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction and Talairach coordinates (tables/figures). Preprocessing, field strength (3T), and analysis software (BrainVoyager) are described. Full article text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (natural rewards), with clear within-participant contrasts (food vs. objects and high- vs low-palatable foods). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported with small-volume (ROI) cluster-size correction and peak coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Results and methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using monetary cues in a visual MID task (visual cue component) and assesses reward-related cue-reactivity (monetary gain/loss cues). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., gain cue > neutral cue; loss cue > neutral cue) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses using whole-brain BPM with small-volume correction (SVC) in predefined VOIs, with SVC-adjusted FWE-corrected results. Participant/sample details, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual food pictures (natural reward cues) and a within-subject contrast of food pictures > location pictures. Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) are reported with voxelwise cluster results shown in tables/figures (whole-brain voxelwise inference with reported thresholds and coordinates). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective (visual natural reward cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts; the study is empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is complete. This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug cues: participants performed a financial market decision-making task after smoking (nicotine/placebo) rather than being exposed to visual drug or natural reward cues. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component) nor I4 (within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli). The paper does satisfy inclusion aspects I5 (reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain and small-volume-corrected results), I6 (reports voxelwise results in figures/tables), and I7 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual reward cues (Monetary Incentive Delay task) comparing reward vs. neutral cues within participants, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE correction). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI, and preprocessing/statistics (SPM12). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of high- and low-calorie foods). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing high-calorie versus low-calorie food cues (e.g., snack go > vegetable go) and nogo>go contrasts, with group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Z>2.3, cluster p<0.05 corrected). Results are reported in tables/figures with MNI coordinates and ROI follow-ups. Methods report participant age/sex, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used visual Pavlovian cues (fractal images) predicting monetary reward/loss and reported group-level voxelwise task results (incongruent vs congruent contrasts and behavioural covariate correlations; whole-brain coordinate tables are provided). Thus it meets I3 (visual reward-related cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (coordinates/figures reported), and I7 (participant age/sex, MRI field strength and preprocessing/software reported). However, it does NOT report a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast for drug cues or for natural reward cues (e.g., appetitive Pavlovian cue > neutral) as required by I4; the alcohol/water background trials were explicitly disregarded in the main analyses (and any alcohol-picture analyses are only secondary/exploratory in supporting information). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (sexual) and monetary cue-conditioning using visual stimuli, and contains task-evoked voxelwise group-level results. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing Sexual and Monetary outcomes/stimuli to Neutral controls (e.g., Sexual>Neutral; Monetary>Neutral) and reports whole-brain cluster-corrected FWE results and small-volume-corrected (SVC FWE) ROI results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol, polydrug and marijuana picture cues and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise BOLD contrasts (meeting I3, I5, I6, and I7), the reported analyses contrast non-studied versus studied items within the same drug cue categories rather than a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (e.g., drug > neutral or non-drug). Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) stimuli (videos and pictures) with within-participant contrasts of erotic > non-erotic stimuli. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM5 with whole-brain results reported (including FDR-corrected maps and thresholded statistical maps and cluster coordinates). Essential reporting details (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity meta-analysis of visual natural rewards and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues and includes within-participant contrasts (mSEX > neutral; mSEX > aversive). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (FWE pcorr < 0.05) with peak coordinates (Table 1) and an exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected activation (right inferior occipital gyrus). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual graphical cues (food baskets/wallet cues). It includes a within-participant contrast of high vs. no food reward (anticipation_high) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using small-volume correction in the ventral striatum (SVC coordinates and cluster stats reported). Voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and participant demographics are described. The full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of high- and low-energy foods). The study reports within-participant cue contrasts (nogo_dessert vs rest and nogo_vegetable vs rest) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses reported at p=0.001, k=8) with reported peak regions/tables, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of highly desirable > less desirable food images and all food > non-food images at the first level, and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain paired t-test with coordinates and p-values, as well as small-volume-corrected analyses for insula and putamen). Necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, 3-T MRI field strength, preprocessing with SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes the required within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic video stimuli (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (erotic vs sport control). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported, including small-volume correction (hypothalamus) and voxelwise correlations between BOLD (erotic>sport) and individual measures. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager 4.9) are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for natural reward visual cue-reactivity (I3), a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (I5–I6); reporting details satisfy I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual monetary reward cues (ring of dollar signs vs neutral cue) during a rewarded antisaccade task in abstinent smokers and non-smokers. It includes within-subject comparisons of reward vs. neutral trials (incentive effects and incentive × time interactions), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain cluster-corrected using voxel p<0.001 and AlphaSim cluster threshold; Talairach coordinates and F-statistics are provided). Participant demographics, cue type, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie vs low-calorie images). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie) at the group level, reports voxelwise results including small-volume-corrected coordinates for the basolateral amygdala, and provides sufficient methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI, SPM12/MATLAB preprocessing). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (palatable food photographs) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food>non-food. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, P<.05 using FLAME1), and participant age/sex, cue type, field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are described. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues (static erotic pictures) with a within-subject design (erotic vs non-erotic contrasts). Group-level voxelwise analyses (ANOVA, post-hoc F-tests) were performed and reported with cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates and cluster statistics are provided. Methods report participant age/sex (19 healthy males, mean age 24), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual tobacco-related advertisements as cues (e-cigarette, cigarette, and matched control images). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing flavored/tobacco/control conditions (e.g., sweet/fruit vs tobacco, and comparisons with control images). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster FWE-corrected p<0.05) for sweet/fruit versus tobacco advertisements, and notes exploratory whole-brain comparisons with control conditions in the supplement. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual video stimuli (first-person smoking vs neutral videos). The analyses include a within-subject Cigarette Cues > Neutral Cues contrast and report group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with peak coordinates and tables/figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and stats software (FSL), participant demographics, and cue/task details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation using visual cue videos (food and cocaine) in human participants and reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine>neutral and food>neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed with SPM8 and cluster-level FWE correction; results are reported with cluster tables/coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (4T), cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual anticipation cues for reward and loss, meeting the review focus on natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues. The authors report within-participant contrasts (reward anticipation > neutral; loss anticipation > neutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are provided both whole-brain (task effects under placebo) and via small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (striatum, insula, ACC) with pFWE values. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues) with within-participant contrasts comparing cue types (e.g., ADMIT_TASTY>ADMIT_NOT_TASTY and ADMIT_TASTY>REGULATE_TASTY). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical analyses are reported (voxelwise P<0.001, cluster FWE P<0.05) and results are presented in tables/figures. Relevant methodological details (participant sex/age range, cue type, 3T MRI, SPM8 preprocessing/statistics) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of natural-reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of spicy vs non-spicy foods). The study reports within-participant contrasts (spicy food > non-spicy food) entered into group-level random-effects analyses and reports voxelwise whole-brain results corrected for multiple comparisons (p < 0.05, FWE; cluster threshold k>20) with peak coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing pipeline and SPM12 statistical software. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrast) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie (and low-calorie) food > neutral/baseline, reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with cluster-familywise correction and tables of MNI coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Verio), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT). Although the paper also reports seed-based connectivity and resting-state analyses, it clearly includes qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual romantic cues (natural reward) vs neutral controls, with within-subject contrasts (romantic>neutral) and group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses with cluster-based correction reported. Methods report visual-only stimuli (IAPS romantic images), scanning on a 3T scanner, preprocessing/analysis with SPM8, and results described as whole-brain cluster-corrected activations across regions. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying voxelwise group-level results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual substance images (alcohol/cannabis) in adolescents, paired with an interoceptive manipulation. It includes within-participant conditions contrasting substance images vs neutral/scrambled baseline (percent signal change computed against baseline) and reports group-level voxelwise LME results with whole-brain cluster-correction (AFNI 3dFWHMx/3dClustSim). Significant voxelwise group-by-interoception clusters are reported (whole-brain corrected). Key methodological details (participant ages/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software AFNI) are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue-exposure paradigm used tactile cues (presentation of a marijuana pipe vs a pencil) rather than visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues. The full text is otherwise complete and reports a within-participant marijuana>control contrast (I4), group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with cluster correction (I5), reports results in tables/figures (I6), and provides participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclusion is based specifically on failure to meet I3 (no visual cue component).

This is a task-evoked fMRI study in humans using visual erotic scenes (IAPS) as natural reward-related cues and neutral control pictures; it reports within-participant contrasts (erotic>neutral) in a crossover design. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported (erotic vs neutral, fearful vs neutral) with FWE-corrected statistics, and ROI small-volume-corrected results are also provided for VTA/NAcc/amygdala. The paper provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and stimulus/cue type. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not report a within-participant cue>control (natural reward cues > neutral/non-reward control) contrast as required by I4. The experiment presents only food images and contrasts (e.g., unhealthy > healthy) and parametric valuation effects (bid-modulated BOLD), but no food-versus-neutral or cue-versus-control within-subject contrast. The paper does include whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results and reports MRI parameters and preprocessing (meeting I5, I6, I7) and clearly assesses visual natural reward cues (I3). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual word cues (drug vs. neutral words presented via MRI goggles). It reports within-participant contrasts (drug-word vs. neutral-word) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-level correction and small-volume corrections (coordinates and statistics presented in Table 1 and figures). MRI field strength (4T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain/SVC results), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (participant and acquisition details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food pictures as natural reward cues (visual-only). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing food versus neutral object conditions and related contrasts (food>neutral, attention manipulations) at the group level using random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (F- and t-maps), with thresholding and cluster criteria and reported fROIs/coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cues (monetary gains/losses) using explicit visual cues (colored circles predicting outcomes), with within-participant contrasts (anticipation/delivery of gains vs losses and cue vs baseline reported). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted with small-volume correction within prefrontal/limbic masks and ROI analyses; results are reported with coordinates and figures/tables. Key methodological details (age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, AFNI preprocessing/statistics) are provided. The study therefore meets the meta-analysis scope (natural reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7. It does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; reports voxelwise SVC results and within-participant contrasts). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol and neutral images (ACR task). It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral) with reported group-level voxelwise activations (mOFC, bilateral occipital cortex, PCC) and whole-brain statistical thresholds (voxel p<0.001, cluster p<0.05 FWE). The methods report imaging field strength (3T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical approaches. Voxelwise results are described in text and figures/tables. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain task-evoked results.

This fMRI study uses visual cues (object images) to probe natural reward-related cue-reactivity (monetary and social), includes within-subject contrasts of rewarded versus neutral trials, and reports group-level voxelwise analyses with small-volume-corrected (FWE) results in hippocampus and striatum. The manuscript provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures: high-calorie, low-calorie, non-food) addressing natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food). It includes within-subject, within-participant contrasts (food vs. non-food and high- vs. low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain FWE-corrected findings and ROI/SVC analyses (coordinates, tables, and figures referenced). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistics (SPM12, details provided), and participant demographics. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, presents task-evoked within-participant contrasts). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not provide any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of a natural reward with a clear visual cue—the yellow light paired with juice), I4 (within-participant event contrasts comparing cue vs other event types), and I7 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using explicit visual sexual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing sexual > neutral pictures (Sex LO > Neutral LO and Sex PC > Neutral PC). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: ROI-based small-volume-corrected analyses (anatomical masks, p < .05 FWE-corrected) and whole-brain analyses are available in the supplementary material. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual stimuli (graphic cigarette warning labels) related to a drug (tobacco) and assessing neural and behavioral responses. It includes within-participant contrasts of LABEL>CONTROL and HIGH>LOW, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and provides tables/figures of coordinate results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. Although the stimuli are aversive warning images rather than appetitive drug paraphernalia, they are clearly drug-related visual cues and modulate craving, fitting the review’s scope. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (water-related and drug-related pictures) in active heroin users. It reports within-subject contrasts (Thirst > Neutral and Drug > Neutral) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM2 second-level one-sample t-tests, with voxelwise thresholds and Talairach coordinates reported. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only results, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural (food) reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (images of milkshake and water). It includes within-participant contrasts (anticipated milkshake > anticipated tasteless solution; milkshake intake > tasteless solution). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were reported with cluster-wise correction (P < 0.05 corrected) and stereotactic coordinates in Table 2; additionally, a more-sensitive ROI (striatum) analysis was performed. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI tools described) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual food images, with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs objects, low-calorie vs objects, high vs low). Although primary analyses include ROI averages, the paper also reports an exploratory whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise analysis with cluster correction (FSL; Z=2.3, cluster P<0.05) identifying significant clusters associated with BMI z-score change. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), and I6 (voxelwise results presented in main text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) and control (neutral/disgust) stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of erotic > neutral and erotic > disgust (I4 satisfied) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain analyses and voxel-level correction (I5 satisfied). The paradigm is visual-only and thus meets the visual cue requirement (I3). The paper describes voxelwise results in the main text and (implicitly) in figures/tables (I6 satisfied). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported (I7 satisfied). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (pictures and videos) with matched neutral control stimuli. The authors computed within-participant contrasts of smoking>control (e.g., BEGIN S2-T2, END S4-T4) and performed group-level voxelwise second-level analyses, reporting activations/deactivations in tables and figures. ROI analyses were performed with small-volume correction procedures; MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing steps, and software (SPM5) are described, and participant demographics/groups are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual stimuli (hedonic food images) with a within-participant contrast (hedonic food > non-food objects). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with corrected cluster thresholds, and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis is also presented. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, 3.0T field strength, preprocessing with SPM5) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of monetary (natural) reward using visually presented stimuli (card-guessing task) that includes a within-participant contrast of reward anticipation>baseline (a cue>control contrast) and reward outcome>baseline. Group-level voxelwise results are reported within an anatomically defined ventral striatum ROI with small-volume/FWE correction and peak coordinates provided. The paper reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Thus it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast in anticipation), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise group results), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (participant/MRI/method details). It does not meet any exclusion criteria: results are not ROI-only without voxelwise correction (small-volume correction applied), not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and not only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual heroin-related cues (pictorial block design) and reports a within-participant contrast (heroin-related > neutral). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using FSL/FLAME with whole-brain cluster correction (z threshold and cluster probability) and results are described in tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images. The study reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food (food versus non-food images) at the group level, with voxelwise whole-brain analyses and voxel- and cluster-wise FDR correction, and provides peak coordinates and figures. Methods report participant age/sex (female), cue type (food images), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (XBAM). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.
