This study is excluded because it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward cues > control stimuli (no food vs neutral/non-food cue contrast is reported), so it fails inclusion criterion I4. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI study with clear visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues (erotic videos) with within-participant erotic>sports contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed and reported (SPM random-effects, whole-brain contrasts thresholded at P<0.001), and results are presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics (female, ages 18–30), cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99/SPM2) are reported. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of smoking that includes visual smoking images and reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise results for an interoception task and resting-state seed connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (smoking cue images used in a Smoking Pleasantness task), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported for the Interoceptive Attention task), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI, and software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 — there is no within-participant voxelwise contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (no smoking-cue>neutral cue fMRI contrast reported; the SP task produced behavioral pleasantness ratings but no cue-reactivity voxelwise activation map). No exclusion criteria from the review list (E3–E6) are directly triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires a within-subject cue>control task-evoked voxelwise contrast, this study must be excluded.

This study uses an fMRI MIDT with visual monetary reward cues (satisfies I3) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation (A2 win/A2 loss) relative to implicit baseline (satisfies I4). However, the main text reports ROI-based analyses (NAc, insula, MPFC) and does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results with coordinates or SVC-corrected statistics. Although an exploratory whole-brain analysis is mentioned (see supplement), no qualifying voxelwise results are provided in the supplied full text and the supplement content is not available here. Therefore the study effectively reports only ROI results in the accessible text, triggering exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses, no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Inclusion criterion I5 (group-level voxelwise result) is not met. Excluded for E3; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4; inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an original human fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in an implicit approach-avoidance task, directly addressing cue-reactivity. The analysis includes within-subject contrasts that compare alcohol versus soft-drink control stimuli within the approach/avoid framework (interaction and separate approach>avoid contrasts reported). Group-level voxelwise results are reported and corrected using small-volume correction (SVC) with FWE (p<0.05) in a priori ROIs (NAcc, mPFC, amygdala), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Methods report participant age/sex information, cue type, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses without voxelwise SVC, connectivity-only analyses, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrast) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues > control stimuli (High-calorie vs. cars; Low-calorie vs. cars; HiCal vs LoCal). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses were performed using SPM8 and reported with MNI coordinates and p-values (voxelwise results in ROI masks and reporting of corrected p-values for exploratory analyses). Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength 3T, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 (group-level voxelwise results reported), I6 (coordinates/tables/figures provided), and I7 (participant and scanner details available). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (participants viewed food and non-food images). Within-subject contrasts were used (highly desirable > less desirable food; all food > non-food) and these first-level contrasts were entered into group-level voxelwise analyses. The authors report small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (SVC, p<.05 FWE-corrected) with peak coordinates (e.g., −34,12,0), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. The manuscript provides necessary methodological details (3T scanner, cue types, sample, contrasts); while not all preferred reporting items (e.g., explicit preprocessing/statistical software) are fully detailed, I7 is stated as preferred only and does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study uses an fMRI task (monetary incentive delay) with clear visual cues (colored squares) signaling potential monetary reward/loss, satisfying the visual cue requirement. It includes within-participant contrasts of reward cue ("win") > control cue ("no-outcome") and reports condition-related BOLD results. The paper reports group-level voxelwise, task-evoked analyses: voxelwise one-sample t-maps with cluster correction and whole-brain between-groups voxelwise analyses for outcome periods, and provides stereotaxic coordinates for clusters. These elements meet inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, lacking within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cues (natural rewards) in adolescents. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood and sweets>nonsweet (i.e., cue>control contrasts), and performs group-level voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses with whole-brain voxelwise inference using FDR correction. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food vs. non-food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) at the group level, reporting voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-level FWE-corrected) with tables of local maxima and figures. Methods report participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (food pictures), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The study therefore satisfies all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic stimuli (natural rewards) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results; however the paper does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., erotic>neutral) required by I4. The reported analyses are main effects (sex, age) and interactions (sex×age×group) and ROI follow-ups, but no explicit within-subject erotic>neutral contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast).

This is an empirical fMRI study using clear visual cues (coloured squares predicting monetary reward) that examines reward-related cue-reactivity. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing rewarded cues to non-rewarded control cues (main effect of reward: (A+C)-(B+D)). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain thresholding and results surviving P<0.05 corrected; small-volume corrections applied to a priori regions), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked analyses. Key methodological and participant details are reported (age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing/statistics with SPM99). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food photographs) and measures cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts (fattening>object; non-fattening>object; fattening>non-fattening) and group-level voxelwise analyses using an ROI-based approach with cluster-thresholding (small-volume correction) across predefined anatomical masks. Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and FSL statistical software). Results describe voxelwise clusters in amygdala, OFC, occipital cortex, etc., fulfilling the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met: it is not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues (IAPS) with within-subject contrasts of erotic > neutral. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were conducted (SPM99) with FDR correction and results reported as cluster/coordinate tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Study therefore meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- and low-calorie food images vs. objects). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods>objects; low-calorie foods>objects). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM8 with small-volume correction (a priori ROIs) and FWE correction reported, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Results are reported in the text and quantified via percent signal change and ROI peak coordinates. Participant demographics (female, ages 19–28), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses visual erotic (sexual) cues (I3: visual natural-reward cues — erotic IAPS images) and reports within-participant cue contrasts (erotic > emotional and erotic > neutral) used in first-level models (I4). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates and cluster statistics (p<.005 uncorrected, k≥10), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result (I5); results are reported in tables/coordinates and described in the main text (I6). Participant characteristics, cue type, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported (I7). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual natural reward-related cues (sexual images from IAPS), using a within-subject contrast (sexual images > matched non-sexual images). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain FWE-corrected cluster-level significance and coordinate tables/figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant age/sex are provided. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes an appropriate within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food > non-food and high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise second-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster correction (Monte Carlo simulations; voxelwise p<0.001), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. MRI field strength (3T), stimuli type, and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are reported. Although ROIs were also used, whole-brain voxelwise results are presented, so the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that uses visual cues (abstract images) paired with food odors (a multimodal design that includes visual cues). The paper reports within-participant contrasts and learning-related analyses comparing food cue trials to non-food/air trials (e.g., faster RTs and greater CS value/RPE-related activity for food vs non-food/air), satisfying a within-subject cue>control comparison. Voxelwise task-evoked results are reported at the group level with whole-brain FDR-corrected maps (and SVC in the hippocampus); statistical maps are available on NeuroVault, meeting the whole-brain/SVC requirement. The manuscript provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text is complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This empirical task-based fMRI study used visual alcohol cues (alcohol images) and neutral/control images, and computed within-subject contrasts of cue>control (e.g., [attend alcohol > attend neutral]). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain analyses at p<0.05 FWE and peak coordinates/figures), with preprocessing and software (SPM8/12) and MRI field strength (3T) described. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual-only video cues (segments of the Internet video game) and neutral control stimuli, with within-subject contrasts of game cues > neutral. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported as whole-brain clusters with Talairach coordinates and FDR correction (cluster-wise thresholding), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected statistical results. Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing/statistical software Brain Voyager). The paradigm assesses natural reward–related cue-reactivity (video game cues) and thus matches the meta-analysis objective. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pornographic vs neutral pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts of explicit>neutral (explicit/neutral regressors at subject level) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses reported with cluster-level FWE correction and peak coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3T Siemens), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), participant demographics (age, all male), and cue type. Results provide whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked findings and coordinate tables/figures and also acceptable PPI connectivity analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; contains task-evoked voxelwise results; includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards.

This study investigates visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, but it does NOT include a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images). Instead, contrasts compare task states with the same food stimuli (inhibition vs passive viewing, imaginary eating vs passive viewing, and inhibition vs imaginary eating). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward, visual food cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported, FDR-corrected), I6 (coordinates/figures reported), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). Exclusion criterion triggered: E5 (only between-condition/task contrasts without a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because no within-subject natural reward>control cue contrast (I4 not met).

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It reports first-level cue contrasts (highly desirable > less desirable food images) and group-level voxelwise paired t-test comparing walnut vs. placebo, with stereotactic coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected results (right insula: X,Y,Z 32,10,10; p<.003 FWE cluster), and provides MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) and participant demographics. All required reporting for inclusion is present and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It contains a within-participant contrast (food > non-food) analyzed at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain statistics (one-sample t-test; voxelwise p=0.001, cluster-level FDR Q<0.05) and reports activated clusters with MNI coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli in overweight/obese participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of food images > non-food images and high-calorie > low-calorie images. The study reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain voxelwise analyses and masked voxelwise analyses within ROIs / small-volume approaches), along with ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (high/low calorie food images, non-food), MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Although many drug-related contrasts yielded null findings, the presence of group-level voxelwise results satisfies the requirement for inclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural (food) reward processing using an incentive delay task with explicit visual cues (basket/wallet images) cueing potential reward. The study reports within-participant contrasts contrasting anticipation of high reward versus no-reward (anticipation_high) and receipt_high versus no-receipt, i.e., cue>control contrasts. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (results reported at voxelwise P<0.001 uncorrected, with tables/figures and MNI coordinates). The paper provides participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and task/cue details. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual erotic film stimuli (visual-only cues). It includes within-subject contrasts of erotic films > neutral films across menstrual phases. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (mixed-effects FLAME stages 1+2) with cluster-based thresholding (Z>2.3, p<0.05 corrected), reporting activation maps/clusters, and results are described in the main text/figures. Key methodological details (participant sex/age, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing/statistical software FSL) are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related and neutral images (visual cue component) in heroin-dependent patients and controls. It includes within-participant contrasts (BOLD_drugcues > BOLD_neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results: whole-brain analyses and OFC small-volume-corrected results (FWE-corrected cluster thresholds) with tables/figures of significant clusters. Methods and results (including preprocessing, scanner, statistical software SPM8, MRI field strength implied by 3T scanner) are fully reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes the required within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study directly assesses alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol stimuli within a go/no-go task. It includes a within-participant contrast comparing alcohol cues to control stimuli (contrast 1: Alcohol_nogo > Non-alcohol_go) and additional interaction and main-effect contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates/tables/figures (SPM8; 3T scanner). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contains qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual drug cue reactivity.

Excluded because the study does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli as required (I4 not met). This fMRI study uses visual food stimuli (meets I3) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results analyzed with SPM5 at the second level (meets I5 and I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported (meets I7). However, the reported contrasts are pleasant versus unpleasant food pictures (food>food), not food cues versus neutral/non-food control stimuli or baseline, so there is no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet inclusion criterion I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic film clips (natural reward-related visual cues). The authors report within-participant E (erotic) > N (neutral/relaxing/sports) contrasts and implemented a random-effects, group-level voxelwise analysis using SPM99. Results are reported as loci of significant activation (tables/figures with coordinates) with both ROI-based thresholds and whole-brain corrected thresholds described. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI task-evoked voxelwise cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards and should be included.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (images signaling alcohol, food, neutral) and reports within-participant cue contrasts (alcohol > neutral and alcohol vs food) during the anticipatory phase. The paper presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results across the whole brain and ROI small-volume-corrected analyses (cluster thresholds, coordinates, volumes, and supplementary tables/figures are reported). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI), participant demographics, and cue details. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI studies using visual stimuli and provides qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original human empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of hedonic food images > nonfood objects, and group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects results with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and coordinate tables. Relevant methodological details (participant ages/sex, cue type, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual monetary reward cues ($ vs #) during an antisaccade task, meeting the review focus on drug or natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity. The study reports within-participant contrasts (Reward vs Neutral) and analyzes reward>neutral effects. Group-level mixed-effects fMRI analyses were run and z-statistic images within a priori ROIs were corrected for multiple comparisons using FDR (i.e., small-volume correction within ROIs), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise, small-volume-corrected task-evoked result. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL). Whole-brain analyses found no clusters beyond ROIs, but that does not negate the reported small-volume voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of high- and low-caloric foods and non-foods). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-caloric > low-caloric; also HC, LC, and NF against implicit baseline) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with small-volume correction in a predefined VTA ROI (FWE-corrected results, peak coordinates and t/z values reported). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies with visual cues and qualifying voxelwise results.

This study is excluded because it investigates nalmefene effects on emotional face processing (angry/fearful faces) rather than drug-related or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. While the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (faces > forms) with coordinate results and preprocessing/statistics (satisfying I5, I6, I7), it does not meet I3 (not an fMRI study of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual reward/drug cues) and does not meet I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control or natural reward-cue > control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) film excerpts contrasted with emotionally neutral film excerpts (within-participant erotic>neutral contrast). Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (SPM99 random-effects, two-sample and one-sample t-tests) are reported with thresholding and coordinates in tables/figures (whole-brain analyses and ROI-based uncorrected results are presented). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI field strength, preprocessing and SPM software). Therefore it meets I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures), and I7 (participant and MRI/method details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual package images as cues. The study reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., viewing regular package > healthier package; multiple package/taste contrasts) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain exploratory analyses and ROI-constrained voxelwise results with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported coordinates/cluster statistics). Visual cue component, participant details (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine dependence using visual smoking-related cues and control images. The manuscript reports within-participant contrasts ("smoke > control") and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (RFX ANOVA and RFX ANCOVAs) with cluster-size multiple-comparisons correction; results are presented in tables and figures with coordinates. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing, and analysis software (BrainVoyager) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural (sexual) reward cue processing using visual erotic stimuli and reports group-level voxelwise results (Tables and SVC FWE-corrected findings). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise results reported, SVC FWE corrected), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (participant demographics and methodological details reported). However, the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli (e.g., erotic>neutral) or an equivalent cue>control task contrast. Analyses focus on parametric modulation by subjective value and delay, and on between-group comparisons/interactions, but no qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast is reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group contrasts/parametric effects without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Consequently the study must be excluded from this cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (Alcohol Pictures Task) with within-subject contrasts of alcohol > non-alcohol beverage images. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain ANOVA results are reported (cluster-corrected to whole-brain α=.05 via Monte Carlo simulation) with coordinates and cluster statistics in Table 3 and Figure 2. Methods report participant ages/sex distribution, cue type (visual alcohol vs non-alcohol images), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5 and AFNI). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (photographs of appetizing vs bland foods) assessing natural reward cue-reactivity with a within-subject contrast (appetizing > bland). Group-level voxelwise second-level SPM analyses are reported (whole-brain and small-volume-corrected ROI results with coordinates and statistical thresholds). Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual cues that reliably predict tastes (visual stimuli signaling glucose, salt, neutral). It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts (e.g., ANTglc > ANTslt, ANTglc > ANTneu, ANTglc > TSTglc) at group level, with coordinates and small-volume-corrected results (SVC) and some whole-brain corrected findings. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (2T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that uses a multimodal Alcohol Taste task with an explicit visual cue component (visual labels 'Alcohol Taste' vs 'Control Taste' preceding each trial), satisfying the visual-cue requirement. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (Alcohol Taste > Water Taste) and presents whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results (Z>2.3, p<0.05) with tables/figures of coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), and demographics are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images vs. scenery). It includes within-participant contrasts (food > scenery), reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using nonparametric TFCE (FSL randomize) with coordinates and NeuroVault maps (i.e., whole-brain voxelwise results / small-volume-corrected), and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study that uses visual food stimuli (natural reward cues) and reports within-participant contrasts (food > low-level baseline and food > non-food). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics, meeting the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. The manuscript provides participant demographics (adult women), cue types (food, non-food, body images), MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistics software (XBAM). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast of food>nonfood, and reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain analyses with cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates and tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/CAT12). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It uses a within-participant contrast of food > nonfood, reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected) and also reports ROI analyses (nucleus accumbens). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager, SPSS), participant sex/age ranges, and cue types. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrast, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual food images (natural rewards) with healthy controls and clinical groups. It reports within-participant contrasts (Food > Non-food) computed per subject and group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests, ANCOVA) with whole-brain reporting of activated clusters. MRI field strength (1.5T), participant demographics (women, age 20–35), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review of visual cue-reactivity and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual sexual stimuli and visual expectancy cues. It includes within-subject contrasts of sexual cues > control (e.g., expectancy of adult sexual stimuli > fixation; picture adult > fixation; child > fixation), and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported as whole-brain analyses with FWE cluster-level correction and peak MNI coordinates and tables/figures. The manuscript provides requisite methodological detail (participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strengths 1.5T and 7T, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The study is relevant to a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards (sexual stimuli) presented visually.

This is an empirical fMRI study that assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using clearly visual stimuli (actual food items presented visually). It includes within-participant contrasts of food > non-food cues across three physiological states (Wtinitial, Wt–10%placebo, Wt–10%leptin). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (voxelwise thresholding, tables/figures of peak coordinates; hypothalamus ROI/small-volume confirmation is also performed). Core methodological details are provided (participant sex, BMI; MRI field strength 1.5T; preprocessing/statistics using SPM2), meeting reporting preferences. No exclusion criteria are triggered: the paper is not ROI-only (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported), not connectivity/resting-state-only, and contains qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (milkshake vs water) and includes within-participant contrasts (picture milkshake > picture water; receipt milkshake > tasteless). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using cluster-thresholded Z-statistic images with corrected cluster significance (Z>2.0, cluster p<.05) and ROI masking (constituting acceptable small-volume/voxelwise results). Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Connectivity analyses are present but are not the sole reported results. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so completeness is sufficient.

This is an empirical fMRI study (N=21) using visual erotic (natural reward) pictures and matched non-erotic control pictures with within-subject contrasts (e.g., bodily>non-bodily; positive bodily>positive non-bodily). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2; FDR-corrected thresholds, cluster sizes, coordinates referenced), and parametric modulation analyses relate subjective ratings to BOLD. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T MRI field, preprocessing and statistical software) are reported in Methods. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts (high-energy > low-energy food cues) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (RFX-GLM) with voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, and reported cluster statistics/regions. The methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager), participant age/sex, and cue types. Full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual high-calorie food images (natural reward cues). It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > nonfood control images, reports group-level voxelwise results within anatomically defined ROI masks (WFU Pickatlas) with voxelwise statistics and coordinates (i.e., small-volume/ROI-corrected voxelwise results), and also presents exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (food) using visual cues (food images). It employs a within-subject design with explicit contrasts comparing food versus nonfood control stimuli and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with stereotactic coordinates and small-volume FWE-corrected (SVC) p-values in ROIs (amygdala, hypothalamus, vmPFC). Results and coordinates are presented in the main text/tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (erotic images and monetary pictograms) to assess cue-reactivity for natural (sexual) and monetary rewards. It reports within-participant contrasts (erotic cue > control and monetary cue > control) at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain results (coordinates and cluster-level corrected statistics are provided). MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM2), and participant demographics (age, sex) are reported. Results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using clear visual cues (abstract geometric shapes) predicting beer versus water (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of beer>water for anticipation, outcome notification, and delivery phases (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs, cluster-level FWE correction) with activation coordinates and NeuroVault links (satisfies I5 and I6). The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only (whole-brain results are reported), not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pleasant images) and visual task cues (potential-win vs non-potential-win cues). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (potential win > non-potential win; wins > non-wins) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (FSL, cluster-based thresholding), with results reported across anticipation and outcome phases. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/software (FSL), participant ages, and task/cue details are provided. Although sex distribution is not clearly enumerated in the excerpt, missing a single demographic detail does not preclude inclusion per I7. Therefore the study meets I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of high-caloric food). It includes within-participant contrasts (Food > Neutral) at the group level (one-sample t tests and group comparisons). The paper reports voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain FWE-corrected statistics for exploratory analyses (Food > Neutral occipital activation) and ROI analyses with coordinate reporting; preprocessing and analysis software (SPM2), MRI field strength (1.5 T), participant sex (female) and cue type are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues vs neutral control videos, with within-subject contrasts (erotic>neutral for both corresponding and opposite orientations). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM02) with tables/figures of coordinates and ROI small-volume analyses; preprocessing, scanner field strength (1.5T), participant ages/sex, cue types, and analysis software are all reported. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Primary reason for exclusion: the study does not include a visual cue component (I3 not met). It used personalized guided-imagery audiotaped scripts (auditory imagery) for stress, favorite-food, and neutral/relaxing cues rather than visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual stimuli. The study does meet I4 (within-participant contrasts of favorite-food vs neutral and stress vs neutral were performed) and I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and cluster thresholds) and I6 (results reported in main text and supplemental tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I3 (visual cue component).

Exclusion E3 applies: the manuscript reports only ROI-based analyses (averaged beta values for nucleus accumbens and caudate putamen) and follow-up GLMs on ROI data; no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts are reported, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI of reward-related cues using a visual Monetary Incentive Delay task), I4 (within-participant reward>neutral contrasts), I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength 3T, and preprocessing/statistics software SPM5 reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and within-subject heroin-related vs. neutral contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (paired t-tests) with coordinates/clusters and ROI follow-up, meeting the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing/statistical software SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to visual drug rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The full text describes a cue-reactivity task contrasting high-calorie food pictures versus neutral control pictures and reports voxel-wise, group-level statistical results (voxel clusters, peak coordinates, t-values, FWE-correction) from whole-brain analyses. Participant characteristics, MRI field strength(s), preprocessing and analysis software are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) versus non‑erotic control stimuli with within‑participant contrasts (erotic > non‑erotic). Group‑level random‑effects voxelwise analyses were performed in SPM5 and report whole‑brain results with cluster and voxel thresholds and some FWE‑corrected coordinates; coordinates/tables are provided. Visual cue component is explicit. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study using visual drug cues (cocaine words) with a within-subject CW vs NW contrast. The authors performed group-level voxelwise SPM12 second-level analyses (one-sample t-test) for the CW minus NW contrast and report voxelwise cluster results (uncorrected clusters used and tabulated) and used these for ROI/DCM selection. Key methodological details are reported (participant demographics, cue type, 3T scanner, preprocessing and software). Although corrected whole-brain significance was not found, a group-level voxelwise task-evoked analysis is reported, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for task-evoked voxelwise results. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI investigation using the Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task, which uses clear visual cues signaling monetary (natural) rewards versus neutral cues. It includes a within-participant contrast of monetary reward anticipation > neutral anticipation. Analyses are whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise group-level results (with peak coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Key methodological details (participant age range, sex considerations, 3-T MRI, and FSL preprocessing/software) and cue type are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not solely connectivity, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (visual + auditory multimodal paradigm) and within-subject contrasts (high- vs low-calorie and food vs non-food). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were reported (SPM8, cluster-extent thresholding with corrected P<0.05) and results are presented as statistical maps/clusters. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study comparing within-participant responses to high-calorie taste cues versus water (natural reward-related cue>control contrast), reporting whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (cluster-corrected maps and peak locations). Although the primary sensory modality is gustatory, the design includes a visual component (on-screen instructions concurrent with cue delivery), making it a multimodal cue-reactivity study with a clear visual cue element. The paper provides necessary methodological details (3T scanner, preprocessing with FSL/FEAT, TR/TE, participant age range, cue types) and reports PPI connectivity as a secondary analysis but also includes task-evoked voxelwise contrasts required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study examines fMRI responses to visual natural reward cues (high-calorie food images) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics for the main effect of cognitive strategy; participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and preprocessing/software are reported. However, it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food cues > neutral/control stimuli) at the group-level voxelwise or small-volume-corrected level. The primary voxelwise analysis tested differences among cognitive control strategies (up-regulation, suppression, reappraisal) and explicitly excluded the passive viewing condition from that ANOVA; passive viewing consisted of food pictures without a neutral non-food control, so no qualifying cue>control contrast is available. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, which precludes inclusion despite other criteria being satisfied.

This study uses an fMRI reward-based spatial learning task with a virtual radial maze and monetary rewards, not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting drug or natural reward-related visual cues. It therefore does not meet I3 (assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a visual cue component) nor I4 (having a within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control or natural-reward-related-cues>control). The paper does report group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain and small-volume-corrected) and provides coordinates and participant details, satisfying I5, I6, and I7, but failure to meet I3 and I4 prevents inclusion. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (and smoking) cue-reactivity with visual cues and reports within-participant contrasts (drinking cues > neutral cues). However, all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (extracted VS and MPFC ROI effect sizes and statistics) with no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical results presented. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast) are satisfied, but I5 (at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods > neutral control and other cue>control contrasts). Group-level voxelwise statistical results are reported (whole-brain analyses with thresholds and cluster-level corrections, and small-volume correction in a priori ROIs), with coordinates and statistics provided. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), participant sex, and cue type are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (high- and low-calorie pictures) in humans, satisfying the meta-analysis scope. The study includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods > cars; high- vs low-calorie foods) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using SPM2 with small-volume correction (SVC) for ROIs (p<.01, extent threshold), and provides coordinate-based activation results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes qualifying within-subject contrasts).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (positive social IAPS images) with within-participant contrast positive>neutral. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (cluster-corrected maps reported; Figure 4) and extracts ROI estimates; preprocessing and analysis software and MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio; Nipype/FSL/FreeSurfer/ANTs) and participant demographics are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and the preferred reporting elements in I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used visual alcohol-related pictures (I3). It reports within-participant task contrasts (alcohol-related pictures > neutral) used for ROI definition and group analyses (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (voxelwise t-tests, corrected thresholds such as Bonferroni/FWE, T-scores, cluster sizes and Talairach coordinates) satisfying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected evidence (I5). Results and coordinates are presented in the main text/figures (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (TurboBrainVoyager, BrainVoyager, AFNI, FSL) are reported (I7). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Sample sizes are small (pilot), but that does not violate inclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI with erotic visual stimuli (natural reward) but did not include a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4 not met) nor report a task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast (I5 not met). Instead, analyses are based on ICA-derived functional connectivity and between-group comparisons of network Z-maps (connectivity), which corresponds to exclusion criteria E4 (connectivity/ICA-only without qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (only between-group contrasts without within-participant cue>control contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cue; erotic video) and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) with visual-word cues and within-subject food vs. neutral comparisons, but the imaging results are reported as graph-theoretic connectivity/local-efficiency measures and an ROI sphere analysis rather than a group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Therefore it does not provide the required voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (I5 not met). Exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses/no qualifying voxelwise result) and E4 (connectivity-based analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts (food > nonfood; high-calorie > low-calorie) and interaction effects pre/post DMPA. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (Z>2.3, cluster-corrected p<.05), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Relevant details (participant sex/age range, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software FSL) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in children. It used a within-subject crossover design with modeled regressors for high- and low-calorie food blocks and blurred control images as an implicit baseline, and reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (ANOVA with cluster correction) including stimulus main effects and activity×stimulus interactions. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, ANTs) are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, within-participant cue contrasts, and qualifying group-level voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual cue-based Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task (shapes signaling monetary gains/losses), constituting natural reward-related cue reactivity. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of reward-anticipation versus non-incentive (cue>control) and outcome contrasts. Group-level voxelwise statistical maps are presented and reported with familywise error correction (whole-brain voxelwise results and voxelwise t-tests), and VOI analyses supplement these results; figures and tables are referenced. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

Full text is a human fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (clusters/coordinates) and resting-state/seed analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues: food images), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). However, the study does not include a within-participant contrast of cue>control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food control) required by I4: instead contrasts compare approach vs. avoidance responses to food (push vs. pull) and pre/post training effects. The authors explicitly note they did not include neutral non-food images. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual natural reward stimuli (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food cues versus control (nature scenes). The authors generated subject-level food>control contrast images and submitted them to a second-level (group) voxelwise analysis (group T-map), and also report small-volume ROI analyses of the IFG; therefore qualifying group-level voxelwise results are indicated. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes a within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity that includes a visual cue paradigm (appetizing > unappetizing food images) and within-participant contrasts. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and significant activations are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster correction. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI acquisition parameters, preprocessing, and software are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The authors performed within-participant contrasts comparing palatable foods to neutral foods and non-food items, and conducted group-level voxelwise analyses (multiple regressions) across the whole brain with family-wise error correction. They report a significant FWE-corrected cluster (right superior frontal gyrus) with coordinates and p-value, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and SPM8, participant characteristics (adolescents/young adults), and cue types. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts (alcohol-cue vs neutral, stress vs neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results with cluster-based FWE correction (p<0.001, cluster p<0.05; supplementary tables/figures). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BioImageSuite, AFNI). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7).

This study used an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay Task to examine reward/loss processing with monetary cues, not drug cues or prototypical natural reward cues (e.g., food, erotic stimuli). Inclusion: I5 is satisfied (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction and reported coordinates), I6 is satisfied (coordinates and ROI results reported in main text/tables), and I7 is satisfied (participant demographics and methodological details reported). Exclusion: none of E3–E6 apply. Not satisfied: I3 (study does not assess drug- or clearly defined natural reward-related cue-reactivity; stimuli are monetary task cues rather than drug or natural-reward cue images) and I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control as required by the review scope). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s scope for drug or natural reward cue-reactivity and is excluded.

This study does not meet the key within-participant cue>control contrast requirement for reward-related cue-reactivity. While it is a high-resolution fMRI study using visual conditioned stimuli (fractals) that include monetary win cues (I3) and it reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (small-volume-corrected pallidal activation for shock CS value) (I5), as well as acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I6) and participant/method details (I7), it does not present a qualifying within-subject contrast of natural reward (win) cues > control stimuli: win-related habenula responses were not significant and whole-brain/task-evoked win contrasts did not yield significant activations (high-vs-low win showed only a trend), and the only SVC-corrected win-related result reported pertains to a PPI connectivity analysis (connectivity, not task-evoked activation). Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual reward cues (images of a $100 bill vs a blurry rectangle) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward > nonreward (main effect of reward). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster-corrected threshold z>3.1, p<.05) with coordinates/figures and adequate methodological details (age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a visual monetary reward anticipation task (visual cues indicating monetary incentive) and reports a within-participant contrast of monetary incentive > control (reward anticipation vs control). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain activations described) and small-volume-corrected ROI voxelwise results in bilateral ventral striatum are presented (FWE-corrected). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues.

This is an empirical fMRI study of appetitive (reward) cue-reactivity using visual CSs (colored rectangles) paired with monetary reward (secondary/natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts CS+ > CS− during acquisition and extinction, and group-level voxelwise results using whole-brain FWE correction and ROI small-volume corrections (Harvard-Oxford masks; SPM8). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts; empirical task-evoked voxelwise results are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (monetary) processing using visual cues (cards/arrows) and includes within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation > baseline and reward outcome > baseline. Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim) across pre-specified ROIs and MNI coordinates are provided (i.e., qualifying voxelwise/small-volume-corrected results). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-related natural reward task, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using gustatory (taste) alcohol cues (alcohol taste vs. litchi juice) with within-subject alcohol>control contrasts and voxelwise ROI results reported as coordinates/peak z-scores. It therefore meets I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported, within anatomically defined ROIs / small-volume search), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (reports cue type, MRI field strength = 3T, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, it does NOT meet I3 because the primary cues are gustatory taste stimuli rather than visual cues; the meta-analysis objective requires a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal that include visual cues). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded on the basis that it lacks the required visual cue component (I3 not met).

This study used alcohol taste delivery (gustatory cues) as the primary alcohol cue (alcohol vs isocaloric control litchi juice). Although participants also viewed written CT/CCT statements, the reward-related cue-elicitation was via taste rather than visual alcohol cues. Therefore it does not meet I3 (clear visual cue component for drug/natural reward cue-reactivity). The study does meet I4 (within-participant alcohol>control cue contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster correction), I6 (coordinates and figures reported), and I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of visual food cues (natural reward) using a within-participant high-calorie food > nonfood contrast, with group-level voxelwise analyses within predefined ROIs and family-wise error correction reported for insula clusters (coordinates and figures provided). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing software (SPM5), and methods are reported and the full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets I3 (visual natural reward cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume/FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures), and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural (food) reward cue-reactivity using visual Pavlovian cues (black-and-white patterns). It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts of food-outcome cues versus a no-outcome control cue and compatible>incompatible cue-response contrasts. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (e.g., vmPFC cluster surviving SVC FWE P<0.05) and peak coordinates, meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study presenting visual erotic and other emotional cues (IAPS images) and examines neural reactivity to erotic versus neutral pictures. It includes within-subject contrasts (erotic and other emotional categories > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from whole-brain analyses (mixed-effects GLM, voxelwise thresholds, cluster tables/figures). Relevant methodological details (participant age/sex, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing and analysis software BrainVoyager) are reported. Results (tables and figures of activations and coordinates) are provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- and low-calorie food images vs. nonfood objects). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie>object, low-calorie>object) in premeal and postmeal states. Group-level voxelwise GLM results are reported with Talairach coordinates, cluster thresholds, and whole-brain/FDR-corrected thresholds; results are extractable from text/figures. MRI field strength (4.0T), cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX, SPSS) are reported. Full article text with methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text (abstract-level content only) indicates an fMRI study using food images (natural rewards) and relationships between affect and regional activation. This satisfies I3 (visual natural reward cues).
