However, the provided content does not report or make clear: (a) any within-participant cue>control contrast (I4) — no explicit food>control or equivalent contrast is described; and (b) any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results (I5) — methods/results details and coordinate/table/voxelwise reporting are absent. Because the manuscript content is incomplete for verifying essential inclusion criteria, I cannot confirm that qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results are present. Therefore the study is excluded from the review at this stage (fulltext_incomplete flag set) pending a complete full text.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual cues. It reports resting-state network coupling and a working-memory (N-back) task, not a cue-reactivity task with drug or reward visual stimuli, and thus lacks any within-participant drug-cue>control (or reward-cue>control) contrast required for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked WM results/ROI identification) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no drug/natural reward visual cue component), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I6 (no qualifying cue-evoked voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) strictly apply, so exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for assessment.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast (food > nonfood). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (ANCOVA voxelwise correlations, corrected for multiple comparisons using cluster-level Monte Carlo simulation), and results are reported at the whole-brain level. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette cue exposure with visual cue components and within-subject comparisons (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper reports ROI-based connectivity (uSEM/GIMME) and mean ROI activation ANOVAs rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures are provided). Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise group-level result (I5 not met). As a result, it meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses without qualifying voxelwise results) and E4 (effective/connectivity analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E3 and E4; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7; inclusion criteria not met: I5 (and thus no qualifying voxelwise results as referenced in I6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures in a within-subject, randomized double-blind crossover design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of Food-Go > Object-Go and tests interactions with prednisolone. Group-level voxelwise results are reported both as whole-brain analyses and as small-volume-corrected (SVC) ROI results (bilateral amygdala and right insula) meeting voxelwise SVC FWE thresholds. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, MRI field strength 3T, preprocessing and SPM12) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (sexual stimuli) using visual cues (nude vs dressed images). It includes within-subject contrasts of sexual > neutral (nude>dressed) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (thresholds reported, FDR-corrected contrasts and voxelwise maps/tables described). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and SPM02, participant demographics and cue type. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, lack of within-subject cue>control contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual Pavlovian cues (colored lights on a vending machine) paired with natural rewards (snack foods), and includes within-participant contrasts of CS+ > CS− (general PIT) and specific PIT contrasts. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (FWE-corrected) with peak coordinates and provides results online (NeuroVault), and details MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that tests visual alcohol-paired cues (novel geometric shapes) and reports a within-subject contrast [CS+ > CS−]. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (cluster-forming p=0.001, cluster-level FWE-corrected pFWE<0.05), with coordinates/tables and figures presenting the voxelwise results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/FSL) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for task-evoked, voxelwise cue>control contrasts with visual stimuli and is includable in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (images of milkshake vs water). It includes within-participant contrasts of unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless cue, and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction and coordinates. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, MATLAB). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text is not available (page shows a redirect/‘checking your browser’ message); only title/metadata provided. Cannot verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (whether the study is an fMRI task assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component), I4 (presence of a within-participant cue>control contrast), or I5 (reporting of at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result). I6 and I7 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be determined from the available information. Therefore exclude due to incomplete/full-text unavailability and inability to confirm required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-evoked fMRI study using visual cues (colored squares) predicting monetary reward (a reward-related stimulus). The study includes within-participant contrasts comparing reward-predictive cues (CS+) versus control cues (CS−) across task phases, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with per-voxel thresholds, cluster-size correction, and peak coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes appropriate within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (photographs) as natural reward cues, with within-subject contrasts comparing sexually arousing versus neutral control images (e.g., W SN > W D) and a subtractive contrast controlling for clothing factor. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (fixed-effects group analysis, SPM99) with reported coordinates and corrected thresholds (P<0.05 corrected), satisfying whole-brain/small-volume reporting. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural rewards) presented during scanning (block design), satisfying the review’s focus on visual reward cue‐reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts of sexual vs control stimuli (sex>neutral, sex>positive, sex>negative), meeting I4. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with voxel-level tests corrected for multiple comparisons (FWE) and small-volume corrections in ROIs (SMC/SVC), satisfying I5. The study clearly describes the visual cue type, participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), meeting I7. Reporting of peak voxels/conjunctions and figures/supplementary material is described, fulfilling I6. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines time perception and monetary reward anticipation (performance-contingent payment) using a visual timing task. It does not assess cue-reactivity to drug cues or natural reward-related cues (e.g., food, pleasant images) and does not include a within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control or natural-reward-cues>control. Although the study reports group-level voxelwise activations (whole-brain corrected) and provides coordinates/figures (satisfying I5 and I6) and reports participant and methods details (I7), it fails to meet I3 (study of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual reward cues) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast for drug/natural rewards). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded.

This study uses an MID task with visual monetary cues and reports group-level voxelwise (ROI mask / small-volume-corrected) results for operant response outcomes, but it does not report any within-participant cue>control (e.g., gain>neutral) cue-reactivity contrasts in the present paper. The paper models anticipation periods, but the reported main results focus on outcome (hit/miss) contrasts collapsed across conditions; no qualifying within-subject cue-reactivity voxelwise results are presented here. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task includes clear visual natural reward cues - monetary MID), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported within an ROI/small-volume-corrected approach), I6 (voxelwise results reported as cluster coordinates/figures), and I7 (demographics, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported).

Exclusion E3: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (mean β coefficients averaged within a priori spherical ROIs and ROI-level t-tests) and does not present qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues used), I4 (within-participant food>nonfood contrast), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise or SVC result reported), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement to satisfy voxelwise reporting requirement). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using visual monetary incentive cues (MID task). It reports within-participant contrasts (anticipation of gain vs. neutral and anticipation of loss vs. neutral) and group-level voxelwise results. Ventral striatal findings were corrected using small-volume correction (FWE-corrected) with reported peak coordinates and t-values. Methods report participant characteristics (sex distribution/age table), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water) to probe alcohol-related cue reactivity. It reports within-subject contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation, outcome, and delivery phases and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (thresholded maps and coordinate tables; NeuroVault link). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, ICA-AROMA) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food and non-food pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts comparing food>non-food (parametric and categorical analyses) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with family-wise-error (FWE) correction and small-volume corrections in a priori ROIs (NAc, VTA). Core methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM12) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and a within-subject contrast of food>non-food (F>NF). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (food>non-food whole-brain contrast) and ROI small-volume-corrected analyses were reported; results are presented in tables/appendix and described in the text. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Although MRI field strength is not explicitly stated, this missing detail does not preclude inclusion under the review criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural (social) and monetary reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (smiling faces, coin images). The within-subject contrasts compare reward cues>neutral control and social vs monetary cues, with group-level voxelwise results reported (peak coordinates, tables) and small-volume FWE-corrected ROI results (striatum, DMN, amygdala, FFA). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (SVC reported), not connectivity-only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (images) (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking-related versus neutral cues (within-group t-tests in current smokers showing greater NAcc and amygdala activation) and condition effects (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported: whole-brain corrected activation maps (cluster correction) and small-volume-corrected analyses for regions including DLPFC and amygdala; NAcc was treated as an anatomically defined ROI with reported ANOVA/interaction (I5). Voxelwise results are presented in the main text/tables/ROI analyses (I6). Participant demographics and methodological details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely solely on ROI analyses (whole-brain and SVC present), is not only connectivity/resting-state, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study is a resting-state ReHo investigation of alcohol dependence and does not assess cue-reactivity using visual drug- or natural-reward stimuli. It contains no within-participant task contrasts (e.g., cue>control) and reports no task-evoked voxelwise/group-level results. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state analyses without task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not assess drug/natural reward cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no qualifying task-evoked whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results), I6 (not applicable because there are no qualifying task-evoked results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual sexual stimuli (a natural reward). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing sexual>neutral (and sexual>positive/negative). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with both small-volume (ROI) corrections and whole-brain family-wise-error corrected analyses. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Thus the study meets the review’s scope (natural reward visual cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study uses visual erotic films (sexual stimuli) as natural reward-related cues and reports within-subject contrasts (Disgust vs Rest) at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain analysis with coordinates and cluster thresholds. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2/Matlab) are reported. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual cannabis cues (images) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05) with sufficient methodological detail (age/sex summary, 3T field, FSL preprocessing). However, the paper does not report a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (e.g., cannabis > neutral) as required by I4. The primary reported contrast is an approach-bias contrast (approach-block > avoid-block) and condition>baseline contrasts, but no explicit cannabis>control voxelwise contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Exclusion criteria applied: E5. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy volunteers examining natural reward (chocolate) and aversive cues with explicit visual cues (chocolate picture, mouldy drink) and a control grey image. The paper reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts of pleasant/unpleasant cue > grey image (anticipatory phase) and taste > rinse, with group-level voxelwise results reported and corrected (whole-brain cluster FWE and small-volume corrections for ROIs). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T Siemens) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity visual-stimulus fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food>non-food (participants imagined eating the food). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (cluster-based XBAM analysis with FDR correction) and coordinates/figures are reported. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that investigates reward-related neural responses using a Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) paradigm with visual cues indicating reward magnitude (big vs small). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (anticipation of big vs small win) and submits these contrasts to group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM-style and BOLD voxel-to-voxel t-tests) with appropriate thresholds and reporting of results (figures/tables/supplement). Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I3) fMRI with visual reward cues, (I4) within-participant cue>control contrast (big>small win), (I5) group-level voxelwise whole-brain results, (I6) results available in figures/supplement, and (I7) necessary meta-data reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual cues with within-participant cocaine>neutral contrasts (cocaine minus neutral image contrasts). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded using SPM8 with cluster-level correction; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and in tables/figures with coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (stimuli, MRI acquisition, preprocessing in SPM8, statistical analyses), Results (one-sample t-test, between-group t-test, regressions) and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s requirements for visual cue-based fMRI, task-evoked within-subject contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise group-level results. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie, low-calorie, neutral images). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie and high-calorie > neutral) and presents group-level voxelwise SPM results (whole-brain voxelwise maps and tables of cluster coordinates; voxel-level thresholds reported). Methods include MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Although the sample is small (three genetically leptin-deficient adults) and the group analysis is fixed-effects, the paper nevertheless provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise whole-brain results for visual natural-reward cues, satisfying the review inclusion criteria.

This study does not address cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual cues. It employs a monetary reward (card-guessing) task examining anticipation and win outcome, not presentation of drug or natural reward visual cues. Therefore it lacks the required cue-reactivity design and does not include a within-participant cue>control contrast for drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise/small-volume-corrected ROI clusters were reported within ROIs), I6 (results referenced in figures/supplement), and I7 (participant age/sex and MRI methods reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component) and I4 (at least one analysis of cue>control stimuli for drug or natural reward cues). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list (E3–E6) directly apply beyond non-relevance to the review objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study is excluded for failing to meet key inclusion criteria I3 and I4.

This empirical fMRI study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (pictures of chocolate and aversive/mouldy drink) and simultaneously delivered tastes. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of cue>control (pleasant cue – grey image; unpleasant cue – grey image) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster correction (P<0.05 FWE) and stereotactic coordinates. MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (high-calorie images) vs non-food objects in a within-subject, randomized crossover design. It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie food > non-food objects) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: a primary small-volume/ROI-confirmatory VTA analysis and an exploratory whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis (reported with coordinates and cluster tables). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (tailored appetizing food images). It reports within-participant contrasts (appetizing food pictures > glasses of water; appetizing > unappetizing) and whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (cluster-corrected) as well as small-volume-corrected ROI searches. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM, DARTEL, AFNI, etc.) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual monetary cues (e.g., ‘WIN $1’) to probe anticipatory reward/loss processing (natural reward-related cues). The MID task events were modelled and contrasted against implicit baseline (within-participant cue>baseline contrasts for anticipation phases), and group-level voxelwise whole-brain ANOVAs were reported (voxel-level p<0.001 with cluster FWE correction pFWE<0.05). A priori ROI small-volume-corrected results (insula, caudate) were also reported (SVC, pFWE<0.05). Necessary methodological details (3T scanner, SPM12 preprocessing/statistics, demographics, cue type) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (whole-brain and SVC voxelwise results), I6 (results clearly reported), and I7 (key reporting details present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues (BEGIN/END stimuli) with within-subject contrasts (smoking minus matched control pictures). Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses were performed using anatomical ROI masks with FWE-corrected voxel-level inference (small-volume/ROI-corrected results reported). Participant characteristics, MRI parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported; the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking and neutral images). Methods report within-subject contrasts (smoking vs neutral and smoking vs baseline), and group-level voxelwise statistical maps with whole-brain correction (P<0.01 corrected) and coordinates are reported in tables/figures. The paper includes full methods (participants, MRI field strength 3T, preprocessing, analysis software BrainVoyager), results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI task-based cue-reactivity investigation using visual cocaine and neutral images, reports within-subject cocaine>neutral contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise results (SPM8; whole-brain cluster-level inference with reported coordinates). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant age range and sex composition, and cue type (visual cocaine images/paraphernalia) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue reactivity (palatable foods) that includes clear visual cue components (food images; visual cues predicting milkshake). It reports within-subject cue>control contrasts (appetizing food > unappetizing food; appetizing food > water; milkshake cue > tasteless cue; milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with cluster correction and stereotactic coordinates (MNI), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) and scanner field strength (3T) are provided. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used visual erotic videos as natural reward cues (sexual stimuli), includes within-participant contrasts of sexual activation vs neutral (paired t-tests), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM8 voxelwise contrasts with activation maps and MNI coordinates, reporting clusters >20 voxels). Key methodological details are reported (participant ages/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software), satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study includes a within-participant Food > Activities contrast (cue>control), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (p<0.001 uncorrected with cluster-level FWE p<0.05) with tables/figures of significant clusters, and provides participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study directly investigates alcohol cue-reactivity using visual cues (cue symbols for alcohol, food, neutral) and an established cue paradigm. It includes within-participant task contrasts of alcohol cues versus control stimuli (e.g., high-threat alcohol cues contrasted against high-threat food and high-threat neutral cues) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain results with multiple-comparison correction (AFNI 3dClustSim), satisfying the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results. Details on participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Prisma), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, CONN) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met. No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are met). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) cues vs neutral images. Methods specify voxelwise, group-level SPM12 analyses and report within-participant contrasts (sexual vs neutral backgrounds) and main effects of background (sexual>neutral) with FDR-corrected, whole-brain results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, 3.0T MRI, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results are reported as voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and percent-signal-change follow-ups. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials referenced but not required. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking pictures). The authors report within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control pictures (BEGIN- and END- smoking stimuli minus control stimuli) and conduct group-level voxelwise analyses using FLAME with voxelwise FWE-corrected thresholds (p<0.05). Results are presented as thresholded statistical images, tables of coordinates, and figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of monetary reward cue-reactivity using a visual cue (triangle vs circle) in a MID task, with within-participant contrasts of incentive>non-incentive (anticipation) and reward>non-reward (outcome). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (Z-stat images, cluster-corrected thresholds) and results are presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (monetary visual cues), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) are reported. Full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This study is not a cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual drug- or natural reward-related cues. The experimental tasks are a Stroop color-naming task and MRS measures, and the paper reports within-subject Stroop (incongruent>congruent) voxelwise results, but there is no within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or natural reward-cues > control stimuli. Therefore it does not meet key inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity (I3, I4), although it does report group-level voxelwise task-evoked fMRI results (I5), allows qualifying voxelwise results in figures/tables (I6), and reports participant and MRI/preprocessing details (I7). No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) are specifically met. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete / paywalled (only abstract and references available). From the abstract: (a) visual alcohol-related video cues were used, satisfying I3; (b) a within-subject alcohol versus neutral contrast was performed (reported as not significantly different), satisfying I4. However, the reported main results focus on psychophysiological interaction (PPI) seed-based connectivity (effective connectivity) with the posterior cingulate cortex; no clear evidence is available in the accessible text that a group-level voxelwise task-evoked (alcohol cues>control) result was reported as a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical map/coordinates. Therefore I5 cannot be confirmed and, based on available information, the study effectively reports only seed-based connectivity results, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Because the full article is not accessible, this decision has limited confidence.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural (palatable food) and conditioned (monetary) rewards that used clear visual cues (milkshake vs tasteless images; coin displays). It reports within-participant contrasts (milkshake receipt > tasteless; unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless; monetary win > reward-neutral) and conducted group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with multiple-comparison correction (AFNI 3DClustSim), reporting peak effects and effect sizes. Participant demographics and cue types are reported; preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) is mentioned. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material availability noted but not required. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This study directly investigates fMRI cue-reactivity to cannabis-related visual word stimuli (cannabis word Stroop) and reports within-participant contrasts of cannabis-related words > neutral words. Group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction are reported (peak coordinates and pFWE values for ROIs, e.g., insula, amygdala, ventral striatum), satisfying the requirement for qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results. The paradigm uses visual cues, includes the necessary within-subject contrast, and provides MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts of food cues > control (HC–C and LC–C) at the group level, with voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM8. Results include ROI analyses with p ≤ 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons (FWE or small-volume correction) and report coordinates/clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue reactivity. It includes within-participant food>nonfood contrasts, reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps with cluster-level correction, and provides necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing software BrainVoyager). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > non-food) in pre- and post-meal conditions. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and corrected for multiple comparisons (cluster-based whole-brain correction) with peak coordinates reported. MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager), and participant age/sex information are provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and is includable in the meta-analysis.

This study investigates neural responses to food images (natural reward visual cues) and includes a within-participant food>object contrast; however, the Food Picture task results reported here were tested using ROI analyses (an ROI analysis on Food Picture task) rather than a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result for the visual cue contrast. The gustatory (tastant) task includes whole-brain analyses but does not qualify as a visual cue-reactivity analysis. Therefore the paper fails Inclusion Criterion I5 and meets Exclusion Criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues present), I4 (within-participant food vs object contrast performed), I7 (participant and methods details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result reported for the visual cue contrast). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward) with a within-subject Sexual>Neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses) with multiple-comparison correction (FDR q<0.05) and provides coordinates and cluster tables. It includes eye-tracking and penile response but also standard task GLM results and seed-based FC; the qualifying task-evoked Sexual>Neutral contrast is present and reported. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and processing/statistics software (BrainVoyager) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards using visual stimuli.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol and non-alcohol beverage images (meets I3). It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral beverage cues (ALC-BEV) (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with FWE cluster-correction and peak coordinates (meets I5 and I6). The manuscript provides participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) details (meets I7). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are applicable. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

The study is an fMRI intertemporal decision (delay-discounting) task using chocolate rewards, not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting clear visual reward cues; it does not contain a within-participant cue>control contrast of drug or natural reward-related visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported, including whole-brain exploratory analyses), I6 (voxelwise results reported clearly), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no assessment of cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component), I4 (no within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues>control stimuli). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I3 and I4.

This is an fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay task with visually presented cues (word cues indicating potential monetary reward/loss). It includes within-participant contrasts of reward-related cues (A1 prospect and A2 anticipation of $5) versus implicit baseline, and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE-corrected findings (ventral striatum/NAcc and other ROIs). Key methodological details (participant age/sex info, 3T field strength, SPM2 preprocessing) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (cocaine images) with within-subject contrasts of cocaine-related vs neutral backgrounds. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with voxelwise thresholding (t=4.14, p≤.001) and cluster-size correction (Monte Carlo), and an OR map of successful recall derived from whole-brain maps is described. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI), participant age/sex, and cue types. Although an amygdala ROI was also examined, the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results that meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study does not report a within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast required for cue-reactivity inclusion (I4 not met). It does meet I3 (uses clear visual conditioned cues — slot machine vs stamp image), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, e.g., parametric probability maps and Table 2), I6 (results presented in tables/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex and imaging/preprocessing details). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). However, because the meta-analysis requires at least one within-subject cue>control voxelwise contrast (I4) and this is not presented in the full text, the study cannot be included.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cue-reactivity using visual drug-related words presented via MRI-compatible goggles (visual cue component). It reports within-subject drug>neutral contrasts and performs voxelwise group-level SPM analyses with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction and small-volume correction in the mesencephalon; coordinates and tables are provided. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. These findings satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (visual cues, within-participant contrast, and qualifying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) cues and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results; however, the main reported task contrasts focus on sexual approach versus sexual avoidance (behavioral/action contrasts) rather than a within-participant contrast of sexual cues > control (sexual > non-sexual) or equivalent cue>control contrast required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. The paper does not clearly report a within-subject natural-reward-cue > control-stimuli voxelwise contrast in the results. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded despite meeting other imaging and reporting criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) using visual cues (chocolate pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (chocolate vs neutral pictures) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain regression analyses (cluster-level corrected, Monte Carlo simulation) with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are described. Thus all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity voxelwise results are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of visual natural reward (visual sexual stimuli) and reports voxelwise small-volume-corrected ROI results, it does not present a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., VSS > control) as a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. The reported primary voxelwise findings are parametric modulators of Delivery VSS correlated with individual ratings and regression with s-IATsex; no explicit VSS>Control contrast results are reported in the full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with clear visual cues of a natural reward), I5 (group-level small-volume-corrected voxelwise ROI results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables/figures), I7 (participant/sample and MRI methods reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of natural reward (monetary and verbal) cue-reactivity using explicit visual cues (distinct arrow cues), and includes within-participant contrasts of reward cue > control (mS+ minus S−; vS+ minus S−). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (both whole-brain and ROI analyses) with small-volume correction (FWE SVC) for pre-defined ROIs, satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise, task-evoked statistical results. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (only ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual images of food vs nonfood (visual cue component). First-level within-participant contrasts were computed (food vs nonfood; HEPF vs LEUF) and submitted to group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported with MNI coordinates, cluster thresholds, and Monte Carlo multiple-comparison correction (i.e., qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results). Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T MRI field strength, preprocessing with SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts of hedonic food images > non-food control images (H>O) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FDR-corrected) as well as small-volume ROI analyses. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI, SPM5 preprocessing/statistics) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity.

This is a human task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-subject contrasts (food > object) and reports group-level voxelwise activation maps for the FOOD contrast (Fasted-Initial visit) used to define ROIs. The paper describes imaging acquisition (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), participant demographics, and provides task-evoked voxelwise results (whole-brain group activation maps), satisfying the requirement for at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Although between-visit voxelwise corrected differences were non-significant and much of the main inference used ROI-extracted values, the presence of group-level voxelwise activation maps for the food>object contrast meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual food cues (personal food images) as natural reward stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts comparing Picture versus Word and Picture+Word versus Word, i.e., cue>control contrasts, and presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures. It includes within-participant contrasts (food pictures vs baseline; high-calorie vs low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using whole-brain mixed-effects analyses (and small-volume corrections for seeds) with coordinates and statistical thresholds. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-participant contrast (food > non-food) analyzed at the group level using SPM8. Second-level paired t-tests (random effects) were performed and voxelwise results in a priori ROIs (insula) were reported with small-volume correction (p<.05). The methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant characteristics (men aged 18–60), and cue type (high- and low-calorie food pictures). Results are presented in text, figures, and tables. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cue reactivity (natural rewards) using pictorial stimuli (I3). The analysis includes a within-participant contrast Food > Non-Food at first level and subsequent group-level random-effects analyses (I4). Group-level voxelwise results were reported with small-volume familywise error correction within the fusiform gyrus (I5), with coordinates, p-values and figures referenced (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported (I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-participant contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria, and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food images > control images (separately for high- and low-calorie foods) and group-level voxelwise statistical results corrected for multiple comparisons (AlphaSim FWE cluster correction), with reported local maxima and figures/tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI for correction) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts comparing food versus blurry baseline and food versus non-food (animal) images. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are presented (random-effects GLM, whole-brain corrected alpha < .05) with activation clusters and Talairach coordinates reported (e.g., BA45, BA42 coordinates). MRI field strength (3T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. Exclusion decision because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it does not include a visual cue component. The experiment used gustatory (milkshake tasted via gustometer) stimuli (milkshake vs tasteless solution) rather than visual reward cues. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast milkshake>tasteless), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain cluster-corrected results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded solely because I3 (visual cue component) is not satisfied; the meta-analysis objective requires visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward). The study uses within-subject contrasts (sexually preferred vs non-preferred; explicit vs less-explicit) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses, p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster extent threshold) with anatomical localization. Key methodological details required by the review (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8) are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (movie scenes). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control scenes, and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise results (thresholded maps and a table of coordinates). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI cue-reactivity and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The study used visual appetitive food cues (appetizing food images) and computed a within-participant contrast (appetizing food pictures > glasses of water), and reports participant demographics and MRI details. However, the paper does not report a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) for the visual cue contrast that would provide coordinates or statistical maps usable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. The Results state no significant between-group differences for the picture contrast but do not provide voxelwise coordinates or SVC/whole-brain statistical results for the appetizing>water contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise result reported for the visual cue contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) from the list are explicitly met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (written labels). It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts comparing labeled reward cues versus control/neutral cues (e.g., high-calorie > neutral, low-calorie > neutral; and low vs high), with group-level whole-brain analyses reported (cluster-level FWE correction). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI acquisition and preprocessing, and analysis software are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only or connectivity-only results; results include qualifying task-evoked voxelwise, within-subject contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study using visual food stimuli (natural rewards) with a clear food>nonfood contrast. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (paired t tests using SPM5 with voxelwise thresholds and coordinate tables in main/supplemental material), fulfilling requirements for whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical human fMRI). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This study is excluded because it does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked (cue>control) statistical results (whole-brain or SVC). Instead, the paper reports graph-theory connectivity metrics (global efficiency) derived from fMRI during a food-visualization task and summarizes results at the ROI level (AAL-based averages and PCA). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E4 (connectivity-only task without qualifying voxelwise results) and E3 (reports ROI-level results with no qualifying voxelwise coordinates or SVC results). It does meet inclusion criteria I3 (natural reward—food—cue reactivity with a visual cue component: food words) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). It does not meet I4 (no within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast reported) and I5/I6 (no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked statistical results or coordinate tables). Full text appears complete. Overall, excluded for lack of qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results (E3, E4).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the task uses gustatory (taste) stimuli (sucrose and water) rather than a clear visual cue component. It does, however, include within-participant tastant contrasts (sucrose vs water) and voxelwise small-volume-corrected task-evoked results, and reports coordinates and methodological details. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant natural reward-related contrast examined), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results), I6 (results reported in figures/tables), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (visual cue component). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (natural rewards). It reports within-subject food>nonfood contrasts and both ROI and whole-brain voxelwise analyses, including cluster-wise corrected whole-brain results (P<0.05 corrected) with reported coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are provided. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pornographic pictures). It contains within-subject contrasts comparing preferred (MF/FF) vs non-preferred (MM) pornographic cues, and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction in the ventral striatum (FWE-corrected) and whole-brain cluster correction. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (7T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual cues (pictures of chocolate and moldy strawberries) within a multimodal design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., chocolate picture/taste > control gray image/tasteless rinse) and group-level voxelwise statistical analyses with whole-brain family-wise error correction; coordinates and SPM results are reported. Methods (1.5T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing, participant characteristics) and results are fully described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are presented (stereotactic MNI coordinates for local maxima, voxel-wise subtraction figures), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise group-level result reported as coordinates/figures. The manuscript documents participant age/sex, cue type (visual food images), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, PsychoPy), so preferred reporting items are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual food pictures and non-food control images. The design includes within-participant task-evoked contrasts: food-picture responses were modeled at the first level (food blocks relative to implicit baseline) and differential contrasts (post-load minus basal) were entered into group-level analyses, providing within-subject cue-evoked effects. Group-level voxelwise results from whole-brain analyses (four-way repeated-measures ANOVA) and multiple-regression analyses (with multiple-comparison correction reported) are presented with peak coordinates in tables/figures. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8). Full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie food pictures vs. brick walls) with within-subject contrasts. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of results, and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of desserts vs vegetables). It reports within-participant contrasts of appetitive food cues versus control stimuli (no-go/dessert > go/vegetable and no-go/dessert > baseline) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with ROI-based small-volume correction (T-maps thresholded and pFDR correction across ROIs). The manuscript includes necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Study uses visual drug cues in an fMRI MID task and reports whole-brain and ROI voxelwise group results (with coordinates), and provides participant and acquisition/preprocessing details, so it satisfies I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, the manuscript does not report a within‑participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli in the standard cue‑reactivity sense. The primary within‑subject contrasts are premature>correct within incentive contexts and group comparisons (including drug vs money interactions), but no qualifying within‑participant drug‑cue > control‑cue contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (no accompanying qualifying within‑participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) that includes a clear visual cue condition (picture of chocolate) and multimodal conditions. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of visual cue > control (chocpic vs grey control) and related contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise SPM results with small-volume corrections and peak coordinates. Methods report participant demographics (female, age 20–30), cue types, 3.0 T scanner, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines visual alcohol cues (alcoholic beverage images) vs non-alcohol beverage control images presented concurrently with emotional IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-subject voxelwise contrasts comparing alcohol versus non-alcohol cues (e.g., ‘alcoholic versus non-alcoholic beverage cues paired with positive images’ and vice versa) and reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps with family-wise error correction and cluster thresholds (whole-brain corrected results, tables/figures). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (sexual stimuli) with a clear visual cue component. It includes within-participant contrasts of preferred-sex versus nonpreferred-sex stimuli and analyses of preferred- and nonpreferred-stimuli versus baseline. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim), and presents coordinate/cluster results. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity/resting-state only, or only between-group contrasts without within-subject cue>control contrasts) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI visual natural-reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (pictures) and within-participant contrasts of high-ED (high-calorie) vs. low-ED foods (visual high-ED > visual low-ED and auditory high-ED > auditory low-ED). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed with ROI-based small-volume-correction procedures (ACC, caudate, putamen, OFC) and report statistically thresholded activation (dorsal ACC) and coordinates; PPI whole-brain analyses were also conducted (exploratory). Participant demographics (female, ages 20–27), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI 3dClustSim) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of responses to erotic visual stimuli (sexual reward — a form of natural reward). It includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (erotic pictures contrasted with fixation cross; erotic videos contrasted with nature scenes) and male>female and female>male contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with FWE correction and cluster reports) and ROI analyses; whole-brain voxelwise results are available and described. Methods report participant ages/sex, stimulus type, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), satisfying reporting expectations. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, contains within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses visual cues (pictures of food/money) and includes within-participant contrasts of food>money (anticipation and win), and reports participant demographics and scan details (meets I3, I4, I7). However, the analyses are ROI-based: voxelwise parameter estimates were extracted from preselected 6 mm spherical ROIs and entered into regression models. The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (coordinates/tables/SM showing corrected voxelwise effects). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result) and must be excluded.

The study directly examines fMRI responses to visual natural reward cues (food images) in human participants, matching the review objective. It reports within-participant task-evoked activation maps for food-image blocks (combined low/high-calorie food blocks as the ‘activation to food’), uses those subject-level contrasts in voxelwise multiple regression and group-level comparisons, and reports whole-brain cluster results with FWE correction. Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, 3T scanner, preprocessing in SPM8), and results include voxelwise group-level statistical findings (clusters/coordinates). Therefore I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI cocaine-cue reactivity paradigm using visual images (pictures of cocaine and paraphernalia) and includes a within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > neutral control stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (second-level random-effects, cluster-level correction using Gaussian random field theory in SPM8), providing whole-brain task-evoked results. Necessary methodological details (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength = 3T, preprocessing/statistical software = SPM8) are reported, and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual heroin-related images (I3). The study reports within-participant contrasts (craving>neutral) and conducted group-level GLM analyses using FLAME, presenting group-level activation results/maps for the craving>neutral contrast (I4, I5). Voxelwise task-evoked results are shown in group activation figures (acceptable per I6). The manuscript also reports participant sex (male), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL5, SPM12/FLAME), meeting the preferred reporting items (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast).

This fMRI study used visual food cues (personally craved food images) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, but it does NOT include a within-participant cue>control (e.g., food cues > neutral/control stimuli) contrast of cue-reactivity. The reported contrasts are look vs. regulate and choice effects (regulate>look, look>regulate, yes>no choice), which assess regulation implementation rather than cue-reactivity per se. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward visual cues present), I5 (group-level voxelwise results reported), I6 (voxelwise results available in text/NeuroVault), I7 (participant and methods details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) specifically apply. Full text appears complete. Excluded for not meeting I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of hedonic foods vs. non-food objects). It reports within-participant contrasts (hedonic food cues > non-food objects) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with voxel-wise and cluster-level FDR thresholds; coordinates and statistical maps/tables are provided. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3.0T MRI field strength, SPM8 preprocessing/statistics) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward) and includes a within-subject High>Low calorie contrast. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and a significant cluster (left gyrus rectus, MNI coordinates provided) was reported after small-volume correction (FDR) within the vmPFC; results and coordinates are described in the text. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity with at least one qualifying group-level small-volume-corrected voxelwise result and provides required methodological details.

The study uses an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual anticipatory cues indicating reward, loss, or neutral outcomes, and reports within-participant contrasts (reward > no-incentive; loss > no-incentive). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (cluster-corrected, z>=3.1, p<0.05) are reported, and striatal ROI analyses are supplementary to voxelwise results. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/AFNI/FreeSurfer) are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images versus non-food/blurred controls, with within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) at the single-subject level and group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses reported. The paper presents voxelwise results using small-volume correction within a priori ROIs and reports FWE-corrected clusters, meeting the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results.
