Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanners, preprocessing with SPM8) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a natural reward (food) using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>mosaic (control) at the group level with voxelwise random-effects analyses (whole-brain cluster-corrected thresholds and small-volume correction for the amygdala). Results (tables/figures and descriptions) present qualifying voxelwise task-evoked statistical findings. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and SPM12 preprocessing/statistics. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of emotional responsivity (IAPS images) in long-term abstinent alcoholics vs controls. While it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (emotion vs neutral) and provides figures/tables and participant demographics (meets I5, I6, I7), it does not assess drug-cue reactivity (no alcohol-related cue>control contrast) and does not clearly target natural reward cue-reactivity as defined by the review (the primary task probes general emotional processing; erotic images were used but the study’s aim and design are not framed as natural reward cue-reactivity). Therefore it fails I3 (not a drug or clearly-defined natural reward cue-reactivity study) and I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrast; natural reward>control contrast is not an explicit cue-reactivity paradigm here). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue-reactivity in humans using food pictures (high- and low-calorie) vs neutral control stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > neutral, low-calorie > neutral, utensil > neutral) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM2. Results include whole-brain thresholding and cluster-level FDR correction and also report small-volume correction for a priori ROIs; coordinates and regional activations/deactivations are described. Participant sex, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual (erotic video) cues (natural reward) with adult participants; it reports within-participant task-evoked contrasts (activation during erotic video segments vs rest) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM analyses. Group-level voxelwise results are presented (within-group 1-sample t-tests and between-group 2-sample t-tests) with reported thresholds and activation maps/tables; VBM and fMRI results include whole-brain voxelwise statistics (some results FWE-corrected for GM volume). Relevant participant and acquisition details (age/sex, cue type, 3.0T MRI, SPM preprocessing) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, only between-group without within-participant contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It measured resting cerebral blood flow (ASL) 4 h after ingestion of high- vs low-GI meals, without presentation of visual cues or a within-participant cue>control task contrast. Thus it fails key inclusion criteria I3 (no cue-reactivity with visual cues) and I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Although the paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinate results and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (satisfying I7), it does not report any task-evoked cue-reactivity voxelwise result, so exclusion criterion E4 (only resting/unspecified non–task-evoked analyses) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli (erotic pictures and videos). Within-subject contrasts were computed for male and female pictures/videos contrasted with fixation (pictures) and neutral nature scenes (videos), satisfying a cue>control contrast. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) as well as ROI analyses, fulfilling the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Stimuli are visual (pictures/videos), and reporting includes participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM, MarsBar), meeting reporting preferences. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and tests within-subject contrasts of food stimuli (FS) versus nonfood control (FN), meeting the cue>control requirement. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (ROI-based inference with FDR small-volume correction in anatomically defined ROIs), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. The paper reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using clearly visual brand cues (logos/bottle images) preceding taste (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing cue types (strong vs. weak brands; Coca vs. Pepsi), i.e., cue-related contrasts (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (SPM random-effects analyses, thresholded maps, cluster coordinates in MNI space; whole-brain reporting) satisfying the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain results (I5,I6). Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked fMRI). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic cues (videos and still images) as natural reward stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of erotic vs. control (sport) stimuli in both block (video) and event-related (picture) designs. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (fixed-effect voxel-wise group maps, thresholded and localized in Talairach space), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age, male sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager 4.9, GLM) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI task that uses visual reward cues (Monetary Incentive Delay task: gain vs neutral cues) constituting natural reward-related cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts of gain>neutral (reward cues > control) for anticipation and feedback phases. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume familywise-error correction and peak coordinates (satisfying whole-brain/SVC reporting and coordinate tables/figures). Participant characteristics, cue type (monetary visual cues), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although cues are monetary (not drug), they qualify as natural reward-related visual cues per the meta-analysis objective, and the paper provides task-evoked voxelwise SVC results, so all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual food cues (pictures) comparing functional vs standard foods using a within-subject contrast (functional > standard). First-level contrasts and second-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with voxelwise results and corrected cluster thresholds (Monte Carlo/AlphaSim), including coordinates and cluster extents. The methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM), participant age range, and task details. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of monetary incentive processing using a lottery/feedback task in cocaine-dependent patients and controls. It does include within-participant contrasts of reward versus loss (gain>loss, boost>loss) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with coordinate tables and figures. However, the meta-analysis objective is cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual cues. The present paradigm probes outcome/feedback processing (monetary gains/losses) rather than visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues (e.g., pictures or explicit cue stimuli predicting rewards). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component). 

Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts of reward>control), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures), I7 (participant and acquisition/preprocessing details reported or available). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual cues). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (120 high- and 120 low-calorie food images) and within-subject contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie; high-calorie > objects). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with small-volume correction (FWE-corrected results reported for a priori ROIs), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results. The manuscript provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cues with visual stimuli and within-participant contrasts (High ED vs Low ED; High ED vs Scrambled), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper reports an ROI-based analysis (5 mm spheres around a priori coordinates) and presents correlations and ANOVAs on extracted ROI values; there is no report of group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) in the main text or supplementary material. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise/whole-brain or SVC result) and fails to meet I5. Full text appears complete.

This study uses an fMRI monetary guessing/reward task rather than a cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues. It does not include a within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control. It does, however, report voxelwise group-level task-evoked results within ROIs with coordinate tables and participant details. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue-based drug/natural cue-reactivity) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related pictures and neutral IAPS images (visual cue component). It includes within-subject contrasts (CUEalc > IAPSneutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume FWE-corrected and whole-brain FWE-corrected findings (coordinates, figures, and tables). Methods report participant demographics (age/sex matching), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, BPM). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) video clips and reporting within-subject contrasts and correlational voxelwise analyses. The paper uses SPM99 group-level voxelwise analyses (reported with corrected thresholds), reports participant characteristics (male, age range), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Subtractive contrasts between sexual and neutral/humor conditions are reported and whole-brain voxelwise results (p<0.05 corrected) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (grayscale pictures of objects/animals) that manipulated reward anticipation (monetary reward) and compared reward-predicting versus neutral cues within participants. The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (reward-predicting cue > neutral cue; subsequent memory DM contrasts) with whole-brain thresholds and stereotaxic coordinates, and describes localization procedures (including small-volume consideration of midbrain). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study does not assess fMRI visual cue-reactivity contrasts. Although it is an empirical fMRI study in substance-dependent participants and reports whole-brain voxelwise TMS-evoked BOLD results, the measured task is TMS-evoked activity (interleaved TMS/BOLD) and cTBS effects, not a within-participant drug-cue > control visual stimulus contrast. Exclusion ID met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, and analysis software reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no clear fMRI visual cue-reactivity paradigm), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result for cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it reports primarily between-group contrasts (BEpost-tx vs NBEpost-tx) and does not present an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral-cue) required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis (Exclusion E5). Met inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI with clear visual cues in the MIDT), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported with correction), I6 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures), and I7 (reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics). Did not meet I4 (no clear within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of food>baseline (pre- and post-meal) as well as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results across groups. The methods describe voxelwise GLM analyses, statistical thresholds, and group comparisons (e.g., DEL vs HWC, UPD vs HWC, DEL vs UPD) with reported brain regions, meeting the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a single-case (one participant) repeated-measures fMRI study of food (natural reward) visual cues with within-subject contrasts (food > non-food) and whole-brain/ROI analyses. However, inclusion criterion I5 requires at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). The presented analyses are fixed-effect within-subject contrasts across timepoints (not a group-level analysis across participants), so they do not satisfy the group-level voxelwise requirement. Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant natural reward>control contrasts), I6 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures), I7 (reporting of scanner and preprocessing details). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise result). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered by this report. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not report an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward cues versus control stimuli (Inclusion criterion I4 not met). This study used visual food cues and multivariate/univariate analyses (parametric modulators and RSA) but presented only food images without a clear non-food or control-cue contrast; analyses focus on valence/WTE parametric modulation and pattern similarity rather than a cue>control voxelwise contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with whole-brain and SVC FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results available in main text/tables/figures), I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore excluded for failing I4. Confidence=0.80.

The study is an fMRI experiment of a simulated reach-to-eat motor task using food images, focused on spatiotemporal sensorimotor dynamics rather than cue-reactivity to rewards. It does not perform or report within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control or natural reward-related cues > control required for this meta-analysis. It therefore fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (study assessing drug or natural reward cue-reactivity with visual cues) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). I5 (a qualifying group-level voxelwise cue-reactivity result) is also not satisfied for the purposes of this review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Full text appears complete. Consequently EXCLUDED.

This study used resting-state fMRI (ICA and ACC-seed rsFC) to examine neural correlates of nicotine withdrawal and withdrawal-induced craving; there was no task presenting visual drug or natural reward cues and no within-participant cue>control (visual) contrast. Thus it does not address cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity results. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity task with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level task-evoked voxelwise results), I6 (not applicable — no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although this fMRI study uses visual palatable-food cues (sweet/savory images) and reports task-evoked voxelwise results with small-volume correction, it does not include a within-participant cue>control (food>neutral or food>non-food) contrast. The primary within-subject contrasts reported are Enhance versus Regulate (both conditions use food images with different instructions), which does not meet the review’s required natural reward-related cue>control contrast (I4). Thus the study fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in main text/tables), I7 (participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only resting-state fMRI and TMS/behavioral results and does not report any task-evoked, voxelwise cue>control fMRI contrasts required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (not a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study — fMRI data are resting-state, not cue-evoked), I4 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast reported), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete and was assessed in full.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (infant and sexual images). The design includes within-participant contrasts of stimulus types (infant/sexual vs neutral/fixation) in a GLM. The authors report group-level voxelwise GLM analysis with FDR correction (p=0.05) used to generate activation maps and provide ROI center coordinates (e.g., [−13 10 −8], [11 10 −8], [0 −20 −8]), indicating availability of voxelwise results. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX 2.2), participant age/sex, and cue type are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines neuronal responses to a natural reward (sweet taste) using a conditioned visual cue (geometric CS predicting sucrose) and includes within-subject contrasts (SU expectation > AS expectation and SU receipt > AS receipt). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with whole-brain GLM and small-volume correction (FWE SVC) reported; results are presented in the text/tables with coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-related natural reward reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with within-participant contrasts (appetizing > unappetizing; appetizing > water). Group-level voxelwise analyses were reported with small-volume correction (peaks significant at p<0.05 FDR within a priori spheres), with coordinates given. Methods report participant age/sex (adolescent females), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is a complete empirical fMRI study of monetary reward processing in adolescents, but it does not meet the review’s cue-reactivity requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with ROI small-volume correction), I6 (voxelwise results are reported in the main text/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using explicit visual cue paradigms; it uses a monetary guessing task rather than cue-reactivity to reward-related visual stimuli), and I4 (no within-participant contrast of reward-cue > control-stimulus is reported; contrasts are reward anticipation/outcome > baseline). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails to satisfy I3 and I4. fulltext_incomplete=false

While this fMRI study examines visual natural reward cues (food) and reports group-level voxelwise and small-volume-corrected task-evoked results, it does not present a clear within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food cues > neutral/control stimuli) as required by the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. The primary reported analyses center on parametric (amplitude-modulation) relationships between pleasantness ratings and BOLD activation and group-by-CRP interactions, rather than an explicit within-subject cue>control contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise/small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in main text/tables), and I7 (participant and acquisition details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic versus romantic images (natural reward cues: sexual stimuli). It includes a within-participant contrast of erotic > romantic pictures (qualifies as natural reward-related cues > control) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (FDR-corrected voxelwise thresholds) with tables/coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses an fMRI monetary incentive delay task with explicit visual cues (4 CHF vs 0 CHF) that probe reward-related cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts of reward-cue > control-cue (anticipation of 4 CHF vs 0 CHF) and outcome contrasts (receipt vs omission). Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain results with coordinates) and regionally small-volume-corrected results for a priori ROIs (VS, rAI, mOFC). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), cue type, and participant demographics are described. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical, reports task-evoked voxelwise results, and includes the required within-subject cue>control contrasts. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study using the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (visual monetary cues) probing natural reward-related cue-reactivity, with group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported (family-wise error-corrected whole-brain analyses). The paper reports within-participant task contrasts related to anticipation of monetary reward (A2Win/A2Loss phases) and their Scan2–Scan1 differences and presents voxelwise coordinates/tables and figures. These satisfy the review focus on visual natural reward cue-reactivity and the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Full methods, results, and ROI analyses are present in the article text provided; core preprocessing/statistical software and participant data are reported. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

This is a human fMRI study of heroin-related visual cue reactivity in methadone-maintained patients. It meets I3 (visual drug-cue paradigm), I4 (within-participant heroin-related > neutral stimulus contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported as activation maps and cluster results across the brain and within a priori ROI masks), I6 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables referenced in the text), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study uses event-related fMRI with visual sexual stimuli (natural rewards) and matched nonsexual control images, meeting the review’s cue modality requirement. It reports within-participant contrasts of sexual stimuli > nonsexual control stimuli and preferred > non-preferred stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with whole-brain results (and cluster-level correction) and small-volume correction for predefined ROIs; stereotactic coordinates and corrected statistics are provided. Participant characteristics (age, sex/orientation), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM2) are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked voxelwise results present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images. It reports within-subject contrasts of food cues versus control objects (HD+LD > OBJ and HD > LD) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected contrasts and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis). Participant demographics, cue types, scanner (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cues that includes visual stimuli (multimodal design with visual pictures). It reports within-subject contrasts of high-ED > low-ED foods (1st-level contrasts) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-extent corrected maps and thresholds), with results presented and described in the main text. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2/SPM5, AFNI 3dClustSim) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual food images and includes within-subject contrasts (Food > Non-food; Food > baseline) across pre- and post-meal states. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with corrected whole-brain thresholds and Talairach coordinates, meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant ages/sex, 3T field strength, stimulus details, preprocessing, and statistical software (BrainVoyager). The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses visual food stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, but it investigates neural responses to disgusting (aversive) food scenes contrasted against appetizing food baseline. Inclusion: I3 (visual natural food cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (results clearly available in figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex and methods reported) are satisfied. However, it does NOT provide a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., appetizing>control) required by I4; instead the primary contrasts assess disgusting>appetizing and intensity of disgust (high vs moderate). Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of reward-related cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (complex indoor/outdoor scene images) that signal monetary reward versus neutral outcomes (natural reward). It includes within-participant contrasts comparing reward-predicting>neutral cues during anticipation and outcome phases. Group-level voxelwise SPM results are reported (whole-brain and small-volume/ROI analyses; cluster coordinates and statistical thresholds provided). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM2) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion based on connectivity/ROI-only reporting. This study meets inclusion I3 (natural reward—monetary incentive task with visual cues) and I4 (within-subject reward>neutral contrasts). However, it does not report a group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) qualifying for meta-analysis of cue-evoked activations: task activation results are reported as ROI-extracted NAcc values, while the principal voxelwise results are seed-based PPI connectivity maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E4 (reports primarily seed-based connectivity/PPI without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E3 (task activation reported only via ROI extractions with no qualifying voxelwise activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Full text appears complete. Given E3 and E4, the study must be excluded from the activation-based cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food images) using visual stimuli, with within-participant task contrasts (food>rest and non-food>rest) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The authors conducted one-sample t-tests on contrast images and report significant ROI clusters with MNI coordinates and z-scores (small-volume correction applied to a priori ROIs), and also provide whole-brain results in the supplement. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, MarsBar) are reported. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise results and visual natural reward cues. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This study does not meet the review’s scope and voxelwise reporting requirements. It used a Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task with geometric cues signaling monetary reward/loss (secondary rewards), not drug cues or typical natural reward images; therefore I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues) is not met. Although within-participant contrasts of cue>neutral (e.g., high reward>neutral, high loss>neutral) are reported (I4 met) and required reporting details (age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are present (I7 met), the fMRI results are reported as ROI-based percent-signal-change analyses in the bilateral Nucleus Accumbens with no whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinates provided. That violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing food choices versus non-food choices (food>non-food) and high- vs low-calorie food choices. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain thresholds; peak coordinates and tables/figures provided), and preprocessing/MRI field strength/participant age and sex are described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Although the study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual erotic (natural) and monetary cues and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast for natural reward-related visual cues (the authors modeled anticipation but report outcome-phase results and did not present cue>control cue-reactivity analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cues for natural rewards present/assessed), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), I7 (participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control cue-reactivity contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (explicit penile-vaginal images). It includes within-participant contrasts (PEN>NEU and PEN>BOD) and group-level voxelwise second-level analyses reported with whole-brain FWE-corrected results (maps/figures). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore the full text is complete.

This study is excluded because it does not provide task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity contrasts. Although participants viewed visual erotic (natural reward) and neutral films behaviorally, the neuroimaging component consisted of resting-state/seed-based functional connectivity (VTA-seeded fcMRI), not task-based cue-reactivity. Therefore it lacks the required within-participant cue>control task contrast and any task-evoked voxelwise (whole-brain or SVC) results. Exclusion IDs met: E4. Inclusion IDs met: I7 (reported participant sex/age grouping, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (fMRI assessing cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (task-evoked voxelwise group-level result), I6 (not applicable because no task-evoked voxelwise results to report). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation using visual food (natural reward) cues and reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain and small-volume-corrected MVPA/ROI SVC), and provides participant/demographic and MRI/preprocessing details. Therefore it satisfies I3, I5, I6 and I7. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images vs. neutral/low-reward images). All experimental trials used snack images and the reported contrasts compare regulation strategies (positive vs. negative vs. “now”/allow) rather than cue>neutral control. Because inclusion criterion I4 (a within-participant cue>control contrast) is not met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this rt-fMRI study used visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (up-regulation vs passive viewing; FWE-corrected), it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images or high-calorie food > neutral baseline) that would satisfy I4. The reported contrasts are primarily: (a) up-regulation vs passive viewing — both conditions present the same food cues and thus do not constitute cue>control, and (b) healthy vs unhealthy choice contrasts used for ROI selection but not presented as a qualifying group-level cue>control voxelwise result for the meta-analysis. Therefore I4 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (food vs non-food). It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts (Food > Non-food), with group-level small-volume-corrected ROI results (FWE-corrected SVC results for pgACC and insula) and exploratory whole-brain cluster analyses. Methods report participant demographics (female, age 19–60), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7, and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Results are reported at the group voxelwise level suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

This study investigates neural responses to food images (natural rewards) using fMRI (meets I3) and includes a within-participant contrast of high-calorie vs low-calorie food (HC>LC) (meets I4). Participant details (age, sex) and MRI details are reported (meets I7). However, the reported results are seed-to-voxel functional connectivity (task-modulated connectivity) group comparisons; no task-evoked voxelwise activation (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) contrasts are reported. Therefore the study reports only seed-based connectivity results without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result, which falls under exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criterion I5 (required qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result) is not met; I6 (allowing voxelwise results reported in tables/figures) is also not met because there are no qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual food stimuli (natural rewards) and reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise analyses. The experiment included visual food pictures and emotional pictures, participants rated valence, and the GLM produced category-specific contrasts analyzed at the group level (whole-brain group comparisons with cluster-level correction and ROI-restriction). Results are reported as clusters/activation maps and discussed with coordinates and figures. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type (high- and low-calorie food images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-subject contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise SPM99 analyses (high-calorie > control, low-calorie > control, conjunctions, and subtraction contrasts) with statistical thresholds and coordinate tables; some results survive whole-brain correction. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages) collected at 3T with preprocessing in FSL and full methodological details reported. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (respond alcohol > fixation and respond neutral > fixation) that are cluster-corrected (z>2.3, p=0.05 whole-brain), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise result. Although a direct alcohol>neutral contrast was not performed, the within-participant respond alcohol > rest contrast constitutes a task-evoked cue versus control contrast acceptable under the review’s criteria. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and provides group-level voxelwise results suitable for meta-analysis.

This study does not assess visual cue–reactivity or task-evoked cue>control contrasts required for the meta-analysis. It reports resting-state measures (ALFF) and seed-based functional connectivity before and after ingestion and group comparisons, but no task-based visual cue paradigm or within-participant cue>control contrast. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/connectivity or resting-state analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) applies. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no visual cue component), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), and I5 (no task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results). No inclusion criteria are satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI task study using visual cues (novel geometric CS) paired with alcohol infusion, meeting the review focus on visual drug-related cue-reactivity. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of CS+ (alcohol-paired) vs CS− (saline-paired) (the CS+>CS− contrast was explicitly tested, albeit yielding no significant positive clusters) and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain results (the reverse contrast CS−>CS+ produced FWE-corrected cluster-level results). Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM5), and participant demographics are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Although the CS+>CS− contrast produced null findings, the requisite within-participant voxelwise analysis was performed and reported, satisfying inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related task fMRI study that uses visual sexual cues (natural rewards) versus matched nonsexual images and reports within-subject contrasts (sexual > nonsexual) and group-level voxelwise results. The manuscript reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and provides MNI coordinates/tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (visual sexual images), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The design, analyses, and reported results directly address visual cue-induced natural reward reactivity and therefore meet the meta-analysis objective.

This fMRI study investigates drug cue processing with visual word stimuli (drug vs. matched neutral words) and reports within-participant drug>neutral contrasts and ROI analyses. However, the group-level voxelwise drug>neutral contrast did not reach whole-brain cluster-level corrected significance and no small-volume-corrected drug>neutral result is reported. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task>baseline effects (drug and neutral separately) and uncorrected voxelwise correlations and ROI findings, but it lacks a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked drug>control result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) required by I5. Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug vs. control contrasts were performed), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise drug>control result). Exclusion applied: E3 (effectively only ROI/uncorrected voxelwise results for the key contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (sugared drinks) that employs clear visual cues (colored lights and images of Coke/Pepsi cans) to manipulate expectations. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing branded visual cues versus control visual cues (e.g., Coke-can image cue > light cue) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (SPM2 random-effects whole-brain analyses with coordinates, cluster thresholds, and p-values). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study examines fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural reward) but does not include a within-participant cue>control (food cues > non-food/control stimuli) contrast required by the review. The task presented food pictures only and used comparisons across metabolic state (fasting vs. non-fasting) and high vs. low subjective rating (median split), but no explicit reward-cue > control-stimulus contrast is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. It does meet I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (voxelwise results available in text/figures), and I7 (participant demographics and imaging/preprocessing details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. Because I4 is not met, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual stimuli (multimodal visual + auditory) and reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie (reward) > low-calorie (control) food cues. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (SPM5; cluster-extent threshold with p<0.05 corrected) and results/t-maps/clusters are described, meeting the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant/sample and MRI acquisition/processing details are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients using visual alcohol and neutral pictures. The study reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) during block and event-related paradigms and presents group-level voxelwise results within a predefined relapse ROI mask (WFU PickAtlas) with AlphaSim cluster correction (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results reported as clusters and coordinates in Table 2 and figures). Participant demographics (age/sex) and methodological details (cue type, 3T field strength, preprocessing/SPM8) are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not limited to ROI-only without voxelwise SVC; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; includes within-subject cue>control contrasts; is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and directly compares food>control contrasts within participants. It includes within-subject contrasts (e.g., Food > Places & Clocks; Food > All Other Objects) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons (TFCE permutation testing in FSL randomize). Results and peaks are reported across figures/tables and participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are described. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with explicit visual incentive cues (e.g., text cues “Win $5.00” vs “No Money at Stake”), providing a visual natural-reward-related cue component. It includes within-participant contrasts of large gain anticipation > neutral anticipation and large loss anticipation > neutral (satisfying a cue>control contrast). The manuscript reports group-level one-sample t-tests for task contrasts and refers to supplemental material (Table S1, Fig. S1) for task main effects, indicating voxelwise group-level results are available (meeting whole-brain/small-volume-corrected reporting and permissibility of supplemental-coordinate reporting). Participant and methodological details (age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/software) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity (palatable food) that uses clear visual cues (pictures of high-fat/high-sugar foods) and milkshake cues. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (high-fat/high-sugar food > vegetables; high-fat/high-sugar food > water; milkshake cue > tasteless cue) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholding and cluster criteria described) with reported BOLD results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Although this fMRI study used visual alcohol cues and reports participant demographics and acquisition/preprocessing details (I3 and I7 satisfied), it does not report a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (I4 not met) nor a group-level voxelwise or small-volume-corrected cue-reactivity map for alcohol cues (I5 not met). The authors primarily report voxelwise results for reward (win>lose) and ROI-based analyses for stimulus-category effects, and explicitly state they found no specific alcohol-cue effects; no qualifying alcohol>control voxelwise task-evoked statistical result is provided. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis’ necessary cue-reactivity criteria and is excluded. Exclusion criterion applied: E5 (no accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol and soft-drink images in alcohol-dependent patients. The paper includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol versus control stimuli (e.g., [alcohol pull > soft drink pull] and ([alcohol pull > alcohol push] > [soft drink pull > soft drink push])). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with small-volume correction (FWE SVC) in the mPFC and NAcc, with coordinates and statistical values given in the main text (and whole-brain results reported in supplementary material). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), cue type, and participant sex are reported. The full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying voxelwise results.

This fMRI study uses visual natural-reward (food) cues and reports within-participant contrasts comparing high-calorie versus low-calorie food conditions (i.e., natural-reward cues > control stimuli). Group-level voxelwise random-effects fMRI results are reported with cluster-forming threshold and FWE cluster correction (whole-brain voxelwise results). Task design, participant demographics, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM/DCM versions) are described (with additional acquisition/preprocessing details in supplements). Although the paper also reports DCM effective connectivity, it additionally provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visually presented food words. It includes within-subject cue>control contrasts (food > neutral) at the group level, and reports voxelwise task-evoked results from whole-brain analyses (and small-volume corrections for a priori regions) with corrected inference. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food words), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (only ROI/connectivity results, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity with a visual cue component.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports within-participant cue contrast (ADMIT_TASTY > ADMIT_NONTASTY) showing activation in ventral striatum, insula, and ventral PFC. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (REGULATE_TASTY vs ADMIT_TASTY with whole-brain FDR correction; ADMIT_TASTY vs ADMIT_NONTASTY reported with coordinates). Methods and participant details are provided (female participants, ages, 3T MRI, SPM5 preprocessing). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study using visual erotic pictures (natural reward cues) presented in blocks versus scenic pictures, yielding within-participant erotic>scenic contrasts. Group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) and thresholded maps/peak coordinates (AlphaSim-corrected) are reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software details are provided. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, or lack of within-subject contrasts) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and non-food control images. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing food vs. non-food (main effect of memory content) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster- and peak-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates (e.g., posterior cingulum [9 -39 39]). Methods report MRI field strength (Philips 3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/MATLAB), and participant demographics (age, female sample). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (erotic vs matched non-erotic emotional pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts of erotic>emotional (both anticipation and picture viewing) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinate tables, conjunctions, and FDR-corrected whole-brain results (and uncorrected voxelwise contrasts), with detailed methods (7T field strength, preprocessing/statistics in BrainVoyager) and participant demographics. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete).

This fMRI study uses visual food stimuli (natural rewards) and reports group-level voxelwise/small-volume-corrected results, but it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward-cues > control stimuli (i.e., a standard cue-reactivity contrast). The reported contrasts focus on choice/self-control (Challenge > No Challenge), value representations, and parametric modulators of taste/health during decisions rather than passive cue>control comparisons. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for a within-participant cue-reactivity contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward stimuli), I5 (group-level voxelwise/SVC results reported), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), I7 (participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI study with visual object cues and includes within-participant high>low reward contrasts and group-level voxelwise (whole-brain and SVC) results, it does not address drug cues or natural reward cues as defined by the review objective. The study uses monetary reward (secondary/monetary incentive) and examines memory/reactivation for episodic monetary reward, which does not meet the meta-analysis requirement of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant high vs low reward contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain and SVC voxelwise results), I6 (voxelwise results reported), I7 (reporting of participant demographics and methods). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) applied. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (food and physical-activity images) probing cue-reactivity/inhibitory responses. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing reward-related cues vs control stimuli (food > non-food; active > inactive) and provides group-level voxelwise results obtained with SPM8, thresholded at P < 0.05 FWE (cluster-level) with reported coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistics are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for natural reward visual cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

This fMRI study used visual food cues (I3 met) and reports whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results (I5 met) with results available in the main text/figures (I6 met). Participant demographics, cue type (food pictures), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported (I7 met). However, the study does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control (neutral) stimuli: all conditions are food-related (indulge, distance, natural regulation instructions) without a neutral/non-reward control stimulus, so the required cue>control contrast is not present (I4 not met). Therefore it fails the review’s essential inclusion criterion and must be excluded. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (no accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast).

This is an fMRI study of milkshake (gustatory) consumption and stress imagery. While it includes a within-participant contrast of natural reward (milkshake) > control (tasteless) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results using SPM5 at 3T (satisfying I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not include a visual cue component. Stimuli were taste deliveries via gustometer and auditory imagery scripts; no visual reward-related cues (visual-only or multimodal including visual cues) are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (clear visual cue component) required by the meta-analysis, and must be excluded. Exclusion IDs met: none (study excluded for not meeting I3).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual cues (alcohol-related pictures and IAPS positive/negative/neutral images) in detoxified alcoholic subjects and matched controls. It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral; positive>neutral; negative>neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses using SPM5 (whole-brain voxelwise results, tables/figures cited). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and should be included.

This study used a simulated slot-machine task (visual gambling cues) to examine reward anticipation and near-miss processing in pathological gambling and cocaine dependence. It does not investigate drug-related cues or prototypical natural-reward cues as defined by the review objective, and the within-participant contrasts are between gambling-related task events (e.g., possible-reward vs certain-loss, near-miss vs full-loss) rather than drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast for drug or natural reward cues). The paper does report whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE) and provides results in text/figures and participant/method details, satisfying I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I3 and I4 are not met.

This fMRI study assesses natural reward cue-reactivity to visual food images and reports task-evoked voxelwise results. It used visual IAPS food stimuli, implemented within-participant contrasts (food vs. neutral at first level and paired t-tests for within-group pre/post contrasts), and performed group-level voxelwise analyses including ROI-based small-volume-corrected results (reported left putamen activation). Key methodological details are reported (participant ages/sex, 1.5T scanner, SPM5 preprocessing). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results without small-volume correction, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The study is an fMRI investigation using visual food stimuli (natural rewards) and reports group-level voxelwise results including a small-volume-corrected anterior cingulate ROI (qualifies for voxelwise/SVC reporting). However, it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward-related cues versus control (e.g., food cues > neutral/control images). The reported contrasts are task-condition contrasts (SC vs NSC) during a food choice task rather than a cue-reactivity contrast of reward cue > control stimulus. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used visual cues (photographs of the rejecting beloved vs a familiar neutral face) and reports within-participant rejecter>neutral contrasts at the group level. Voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2, with planned ROI small-volume-corrected results (FDR correction) reported as coordinates and cluster tables; figures and coordinate tables present the activations. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it satisfies: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures), and I7 (participant/MRI/method details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes qualifying voxelwise SVC results). Full text appears complete.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (natural reward: food cues presented visually) and I4 (within-participant food>non-food contrasts). However, the full text reports only seed-based task-dependent functional connectivity analyses (PPI) and does not present group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., food>non-food GLM activation maps) as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only PPI/seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with an explicit within-participant contrast (food > nonfood). The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses with cluster-wise/voxel coordinates and corrected p-values (whole-brain cluster-level inference and coordinate details), and describes MRI field strength (1.5 T), participant demographics (female groups, matched on age/education), stimuli, and preprocessing/statistical methods. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food images (natural rewards). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food versus control stimuli (food > people/nature) entered into second-level random-effects analyses and reports peak coordinates (NAcc MNI 12,9,-3) and associated statistics (t(30)=2.87, p=.007), from which ROI beta values were extracted for group-level prediction models. Imaging acquisition, preprocessing, and analysis software/details (3T scanner, SPM8, smoothing, normalization) are described. The go/no-go whole-brain analyses and the cue-reactivity contrast provide task-evoked voxelwise results appropriate for inclusion. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis’ fMRI visual cue-reactivity inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts of food>non-food and reports group-level voxelwise results. The full text includes whole-brain second-level analyses (cluster-defining thresholds and FWE correction) and ROI small-volume-corrected analyses, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC task-evoked voxelwise results. The methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM12), and participant/sample details. Thus the study addresses natural reward-related visual cue reactivity and meets inclusion criteria for within-participant contrasts and qualifying voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, lack of within-participant contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.
